title: UAV-Based Federated Learning Incentive Mechanism for Latency-Aware Multimodal Target Tracking
content: Federated multimodal learning (FML) over uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) networks underpins privacy-preserving multimodal target tracking, yet energy-constrained and self-interested UAVs, which bear substantial sensing, training, and transmission costs, are reluctant to continuously contribute the high-quality multimodal data on which the global tracking model depends. To address this issue, this research aims to design an incentive mechanism that maximizes the aggregate FML efficiency and ensures economic fairness. This article proposes a novel two-stage incentive framework for UAV-assisted FML networks, modeled as a two-sided market between ground task requesters (TRs) and modality-specific UAVs. A TR purchases inference access to the updated multimodal target tracking model enabled by one UAV’s FML service. In the first stage, we develop a joint latency-modality-aware initial matching (JLMA-IM) algorithm. By constructing an FML-efficiency index that integrates physical-layer latency with modality importance, we cast the assignment as an aggregate-efficiency maximization problem and solve it exactly via a weighted bipartite matching approach. In the second stage, we design a double auction-based winner and pricing determination (DA-WPD) algorithm based on candidate critical pairs to determine final winners and transaction prices. We theoretically prove that the proposed mechanism satisfies individual rationality and budget balance, and that it is truthful under a boundary-stability condition. Simulation results show that the market-driven federated training achieves tracking accuracy comparable to full participation on 114 visible-thermal uncrewed aerial vehicle (VTUAV) sequences, JLMA-IM improves the FML efficiency by approximately 15% and reduces the bottleneck latency by up to 25%, and DA-WPD completes more transactions with higher social welfare than the McAfee double auction.
author: Wanyu Qiu, Fulin Luo, Chuan Fu, Xiao Yang, Qiankun Zuo

title: PT2SF: Cross-Scene Similarity-Informed Point-to-Surface Learning for All-Day PM2.5 Field Reconstruction From Sparse In Situ Measurements
content: Hourly mapping of spatiotemporally continuous air pollutant concentrations remains challenging because ground monitoring networks are sparse, while satellite observations are frequently unavailable due to cloud contamination and the lack of nighttime retrievals. To address this limitation, we propose point-to-surface (PT2SF), a cross-scene, similarity-informed point-to-surface network for all-day air quality mapping from sparse in situ measurements. Rather than relying on geographic distance alone, PT2SF characterizes the environmental similarity between target pixels and monitoring stations using pollution, meteorological, and geographic attributes across multiple scenes. A graph attention network is developed to embed these similarity relationships to adaptively aggregate observations from environmentally analogous locations, including geographically distant stations, to infer continuous concentration fields. Evaluations using hourly PM2.5 measurements across China show that PT2SF achieves an overall correlation coefficient of 0.91 and a root-mean-square error (RMSE) of  $14.09~\mu $ g m−3, with stable performance across seasons and daytime and nighttime conditions. On a common testing subset, PT2SF yields an RMSE of  $12.84~\mu $ g m−3, compared with  $13.64~\mu $ g m−3 for Himawari-8 retrievals and  $28.17~\mu $ g m−3 for Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS) forecasts while maintaining hourly coverage independent of concurrent satellite retrievals. PT2SF also consistently outperforms classical interpolation and deep-learning baselines and shows substantially greater robustness to sparse observations. Under a 500-km station-masking radius, it retains a correlation coefficient of approximately 0.68, compared with 0.18 for inverse distance weighting (IDW). Feature analyses further indicate that relatively stable cross-scene similarity primarily determines graph connectivity, whereas dynamic meteorological conditions regulate short-term concentration variability. These results demonstrate that PT2SF provides an environment-aware and flexible framework for reconstructing continuous air quality fields from sparse observations and can be extended to other sparsely observed geophysical variables using variable-specific similarity descriptors.
author: Songyun Qiu, Ke Li, Zhe Zheng, Xidong Sun, Yuhao Yuan, Ruijie Li, Chaoshun Liu, Kaixu Bai

title: Physics-Aware Multimodal Deep Learning Method for Nighttime AOD Retrieval With Nighttime Lights Data
content: Nighttime aerosol optical depth (AOD) retrieval is essential for maintaining diurnal continuity in global atmospheric monitoring. However, conventional physical retrieval algorithms are often hampered by the low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the single-band VIIRS day/night band (DNB) and the complex variability of anthropogenic surface illumination. These limitations frequently necessitate coarse spatial aggregation, which significantly sacrifices both spatial resolution and retrieval precision. To overcome these challenges, this study presents a novel physics-aware multimodal deep learning (DL) framework, the physics-aware CNN–Transformer (PaCT). This method adopts a standard heterogeneous decoupling architecture to process visual and scalar multimodal features: a convolutional neural network (CNN) branch extracts aerosol-induced texture degradation and background brightening from nighttime lights (NTLs) image patches, while a Transformer-based branch processes environmental scalars to characterize the radiative context. Interpretability analysis via SHAP gradients confirms that the model’s decision-making aligns closely with established physical priors. Sample-based ten-fold cross-validation demonstrates high retrieval accuracy ( $R$  = 0.938, root-mean-square error (RMSE) = 0.077), with 85.56% and 47.24% of retrievals meeting the MODIS Deep Blue (DB) expected error (EE) bounds and the global climate observing system (GCOS) stringent requirements, respectively. Notably, the PaCT framework produces retrievals at the 750-m nominal pixel spacing of the VIIRS DNB and exhibits strong consistency with various AOD products. This study effectively complements the limited spatial coverage of nighttime active lidar along-track observations, providing new data support for investigating diurnal aerosol evolution and enabling refined monitoring of urban nighttime air quality.
author: Yu Sun, Lin Sun, Xiaohu Sun

title: Discriminating Cloud Particle Types Using Ground-Based Scanning Lidar: Theoretical Model and Experimental Analysis
content: Accurately identifying cloud particle types is essential for improving cloud microphysical parameterizations and remote sensing retrievals. In this study, we develop a novel discrimination method for cloud particles using scanning lidar observations near the zenith, based on the theoretical backscattering properties of ice crystals. We introduce, for the first time, the use of the coefficient of variation (CV) and the coefficient of variation difference ( $\Delta $ CV) to quantify the variability of lidar backscatter signals during scanning. By integrating these metrics with the depolarization ratio at the zenith direction ( ${\delta }_{0}$ ) and ambient temperature, cloud particles are classified into seven categories: liquid water, liquid/mixed-phase, 2-D ice crystals (quasi-horizontally oriented), 3-D ice crystals (randomly oriented), mixed 2-D + 3-D ice crystals, complex irregular particles (CIP), and droxtal ice crystals. Meanwhile, based on theoretical analysis, we introduced the high-depolarization coverage (HDC) metric to improve the accuracy of distinguishing mixed 2-D + 3-D ice crystals from liquid water or ice-liquid mixtures. After more than six months of continuous observations, the feasibility of the new algorithm was demonstrated through comprehensive observational analyses. In addition, we also observed vertical layering of different cloud particle types within some mixed-phase clouds. In these clouds, 2-D ice crystals tend to occur in the upper regions, mixed 2-D + 3-D ice crystals are more common in the middle layers, while 3-D or aggregated ice crystals are typically found in the lower parts of the cloud. Our proposed observational strategy and discrimination algorithm hold promise for providing new insights into cloud microphysics, which will further contribute to future climate change studies.
author: Xuanhao Zhu, Dong Liu, Zhenzhu Wang, Alexander Konoshonkin, Zhiqiang Kuang, Natalia Kustova, Yingjian Wang

title: Structural Decomposition-Based Green Tide Detection Under Cloud-Dominated Background Interference
content: Green tide detection aims to delineate the spatial distribution of floating green macroalgae, providing critical support for marine environmental monitoring. However, cloud cover frequently affects optical observations, obscuring green tide signatures and reducing detection reliability. Existing cloud masking strategies often result in the loss of potential green tide information, while conventional cloud removal methods struggle to suppress complex background interference and accurately preserve green tide signals. To address this issue, we propose a structural decomposition-based method for green tide detection under cloud-dominated background interference. Specifically, a pseudo-exposure image sequence is first generated from the original multispectral image to enrich texture details across different illumination conditions. Then, a dark target prior-guided background interference estimation method is designed to characterize complex background responses by jointly modeling spatially varying intensity and band-dependent abundance, providing a continuous characterization of cloud-dominated interference. Finally, the pseudo-exposure images and their corresponding interference maps are decomposed into different structural components, and corresponding suppression strategies are devised to reduce cloud-dominated interference while preserving green tide information. The refined components are subsequently reconstructed to improve the discrimination of green tide from complex backgrounds. In addition, a green tide detection dataset is constructed using Geostationary Ocean Color Imager (GOCI), Landsat 8/9 Operational Land Imager (OLI), and HY-1C coastal zone imager (CZI) imagery under complex cloud interference. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms representative dehazing, cloud masking, and cloud removal approaches, yielding consistent performance improvements across various green tide detectors. The source code is available at https://github.com/PinkSlime/TIDE_DETECTION
author: Zihao Wang, Zhuojun Xie, Qiong Wu, Xudong Kang, Puhong Duan

title: Applicability Assessment of Spherical Radiative Transfer Models for Ocean Color Remote Sensing Under Large Solar Zenith Angles
content: Accurate ocean–atmosphere coupled radiative transfer models (RTMs) are essential for ocean color remote sensing. However, the applicability and accuracy of RTMs under large solar zenith angles (SZAs) conditions remain insufficiently quantified. This study quantifies the applicability limits of spherical RTMs under large SZAs by confronting simulations from two representative RTMs, SMART-G and SCIATRAN, with geostationary ocean color imager (GOCI) top-of-atmosphere (TOA) radiance ( $L_{t}$ ) observations. Radiative transfer simulations under large SZAs are conducted across a broad range of representative atmospheric and oceanic parameters and solar-sensor geometries. In addition, the sensitivity of simulated  $L_{t}$  to key atmospheric and oceanic input parameters is systematically analyzed. Results indicate that: 1) RTM simulation accuracy deteriorates nonlinearly with increasing SZA, with a stronger wavelength dependence at large SZAs; 2) the critical SZA thresholds for accuracy deterioration are identified at approximately 73° for SMART-G and between 69° and 83° for SCIATRAN; and 3) viewing zenith angle (VZA), aerosol type and optical depth, column water vapor (CWV), and wind speed (WS) dominate the accuracy of RTM simulations under large SZAs. These findings provide quantitative constraints on the applicability of RTMs under large SZAs and offer practical guidance for ocean color remote sensing applications in polar regions and during dawn and dusk observations.
author: Yongquan Wang, Huizeng Liu, Yu Zhang, Menghui Wang, Qingquan Li, Guofeng Wu

title: IFRM-CL: Risk-Modulated Dual-Loop Learning for Class-Incremental Fine-Grained Marine Debris Detection From UAV Imagery
content: Fine-grained class-incremental object detection (CIOD) for marine debris requires maintaining stable discrimination of previously learned categories while continuously incorporating novel categories. However, fine-grained marine debris classes often exhibit high visual similarity and subtle discriminative cues, which are prone to degradation during incremental updates, leading to cross-task interference and unstable decision boundaries. Existing methods mainly rely on replay, distillation, or pseudo-labeling strategies, yet fail to explicitly identify and protect fine-grained features that are most vulnerable to forgetting, leading to representation drift and weakened discriminative capability in critical regions. To address this issue, we propose an iterative forgetting risk-modulated continual learning (IFRM-CL) framework, which explicitly models and regulates fine-grained forgetting risk via a dual-loop optimization mechanism. Specifically, the inner loop performs fine-grained forgetting risk estimation by constructing a prior risk evaluation buffer (PRB) and computing a fine-grained forgetting risk index (FRI) to quantify task-level risk from both representation and decision perspectives. In the outer loop, a discriminative risk modulator (DRM) uses risk-guided gating to enhance fine-grained discriminative cues, with stronger modulation at higher estimated task-level risk and weaker modulation at lower risk. Through iterative interaction between the risk estimation in the inner loop and modulation in the outer loop, IFRM-CL forms a closed-loop update process that progressively refines feature adaptation based on risk and stabilizes the tradeoff between stability and plasticity. Experiments on MarineDebris-CL show improved overall detection performance and better retention of previously learned classes in the evaluated class-incremental setting.
author: Shanhua Wu, Dingyuan Chen, Xinyi Gong, Dalin Zhang, Hongbo Wang, Zhaohui Song

title: Mapping of Greenland Ice Sheet Surface Melt Using Calibrated Multisystem GNSS-R Reflectivity
content: Monitoring surface melt over the Greenland ice sheet (GrIS) is critical for understanding ice sheet mass change and its climatic impacts. While microwave remote sensing has enabled long-term melt monitoring, its utility is often hindered by coarse spatial resolution, signal saturation during intense melt events, and diminished sensitivity to shallow melting. In this study, a calibrated multisystem reflectivity (CMS-R) framework is developed using spaceborne global navigation satellite system-reflectometry (GNSS-R) observations from the Tianmu-1 (TM) constellation. To reduce systematic differences among global navigation satellite system (GNSS) constellations, a probability density function (pdf) peak alignment method is applied for reflectivity calibration. Wintertime nonmelt reflectivity is utilized as the background field, and melt occurrence is identified based on daily reflectivity anomalies. Consequently, daily 25-km mapping of surface melt over the GrIS is achieved. The results demonstrate that the calibrated reflectivity exhibits a clearer separation between melt and nonmelt conditions. A significant positive correlation was found between CMS-R anomalies and melt-day counts, with Pearson and Spearman coefficients of 0.76 and 0.75, respectively. Following calibration, the detection threshold was decreased from 3.9 to 3.6 dB, thereby increasing sensitivity to weak melt. During the intense melt event on July 19, 2024, a melt extent of approximately 580 000 km2 was estimated by CMS-R, which shows close agreement with the AMSR-derived estimate of 576 200 km2. Moreover, the CMS-R melt results are consistent with observations from 23 automatic weather stations (AWSs). These findings highlight the potential of spaceborne GNSS-R as a complementary approach to monitoring ice sheet surface melt. The CMS-R framework offers an additional perspective on melt detection alongside the existing microwave observations.
author: Yongchao Zhu, Lijuan Pan, Maorong Ge, Xiaohong Zhang, Fei Gao, Xiaochuan Qu, Kegen Yu

title: Zero-OVCD: Bridging Training-Free Foundation Models and Pseudo-Label Learning for Open-Vocabulary Change Detection
content: Open-vocabulary change detection (OVCD) enables the identification of user-specified land-cover changes in bitemporal remote sensing images, but existing training-free pipelines remain vulnerable to inaccurate candidate masks, ambiguous semantic assignments, and accumulated inference errors. To address these issues, we propose Zero-OVCD, a two-stage framework that uses no manual annotations. In the first stage, training-free, prompt-conditioned open-vocabulary inference generates high-quality change pseudo-labels through complementary candidate-mask refinement, multiscale semantic similarity fusion with margin-based reliability filtering, and response-guided mask correction and completion. These components jointly suppress noisy candidates, enhance mask-level semantic discrimination, and recover missed change regions. In the second stage, a category-specific change detector is trained using the generated pseudo-labels, while checkpoint voting and high-agreement sample selection are introduced to mitigate residual pseudo-label noise. On LEVIR-CD, WHU-CD, and S2Looking, Stage I achieves  $F1$ -scores ( $F1$ ) of 86.25%, 85.82%, and 50.48%, while Stage II further improves them to 88.65%, 88.85%, and 57.96%, respectively. On SECOND, the macro-average  $F1$  across six category-wise one-versus-rest tasks increases from 47.91% to 50.92%. These results demonstrate that bridging training-free foundation-model inference with noise-aware pseudo-label learning provides an effective solution for OVCD without manual annotations. The code will be available at https://github.com/1321663019/Zero-OVCD
author: Daifeng Peng, Yuanke Peng, Haiyan Guan

title: Efficient Large-Scale Remote Sensing Change Detection via Sparse Semantic Scene Graphs
content: Multitemporal remote sensing change detection (RSCD) is essential for large-scale postdisaster assessment, enabling rapid damage evaluation and timely emergency response. Existing RSCD approaches, especially deep-learning-based methods, often rely heavily on labeled data and dense pixel- or patch-wise comparisons, which limits cross-scene generalizability, hinders scalability to large scenes, and fails to capture the selective, object-centric, and spatially sparse nature of task-related changes. To address these issues, we propose a training-free, instance-centric, and sparse framework for large-scale RSCD based on sparse semantic scene graphs (S3Gs). The framework first reformulates large-scale RSCD as sparse instance graph reasoning by retaining only change-relevant semantic instances and local spatial relations, making direct large-area analysis computationally feasible. It then establishes instance-centric correspondence between bi-temporal S3Gs, providing greater tolerance to residual spatial misalignment. By jointly reasoning over instance semantics and relational evolution, it further infers change locations, semantic categories, and structural changes, yielding more traceable and interpretable change maps. Experiments on public benchmarks and the newly constructed large-scale natural hazards RSCD (LSNH-RSCD) dataset demonstrate both competitive accuracy and clear efficiency advantages. In particular, the proposed training-free method achieves 71.65% mean intersection over union (mIoU) on LEVIR-change detection (CD) and the best 78.33% mIoU on the hurricane subset of LSNH-RSCD, while supporting direct large-scale inference on remote sensing images (RSIs) of  $7936\times 9278$  pixels in 42.54 s on a single NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 GPU, more than  $10\times $  faster than the second-fastest baseline. These results highlight the potential of the proposed framework for rapid damage assessment and large-scale disaster mapping.
author: Wandong Jiang, Yuli Sun, Lin Lei, Gangyao Kuang, Kefeng Ji

title: Fast Coherent Integration Detection Based on the Segment RPCA Method for Maneuvering Target in Spaceborne Bistatic Radar
content: Spaceborne bistatic radar has played an important role in target surveillance and reconnaissance for its advantages of broader surveillance coverage, enhanced damage resistance, and inherent spatial diversity gain. However, the bistatic configuration and target maneuverability induce significant range cell migration (RCM) and time-varying Doppler frequency modulation (DFM), which pose severe challenges to long-time coherent integration detection methods. Furthermore, existing integration detection methods, such as generalized Radon Fourier transform (GRFT), suffer from high computational complexity and storage overhead caused by the required multidimensional search operation. To address these issues, a fast coherent integration detection method based on segmented robust principal component analysis (SRPCA) is proposed, which mainly consists of intrasegment and intersegment processing. First, the keystone transform (KT) and efficient center-variant correction (CVC) are adopted to correct RCM. Subsequently, the echo is segmented along the azimuth dimension under the reasonable constraint that the Doppler spread within each segment can be neglected, and intrasegment accumulation is achieved. During intersegment processing, a rapid parameter estimation method based on the RPCA is developed to compensate for dominated higher-order phase terms. Furthermore, the higher-order phase errors are precisely compensated based on the maximum peak criterion. Therefore, well-focused results can be obtained in the range-frequency domain while reducing the computational load by avoiding multidimensional searching. Finally, to validate the effectiveness and advantages of the proposed method, experiments are performed by using simulated and composite data.
author: Xiaoran Xie, Dong Li, Liyin Zhang, Jun Wan, Zhanye Chen

title: Shadow-Aided Sparse Bayesian 2-D Autofocusing for High-Resolution Imaging of Moving Targets in Terahertz CSAR
content: Ground moving-target imaging (GMTIm) techniques present both opportunities and challenges in enhancing fine-grained situational awareness (SA) and target recognition. Compared with microwave synthetic aperture radar (SAR), terahertz-SAR (THz-SAR) offers higher Doppler sensitivity, enabling more effective detection of slow-moving targets (MTs). Moreover, its high carrier frequency and wide bandwidth facilitate high-resolution imaging. However, the substantial randomness in time-sensitive target motion can lead to severe range migration and azimuth defocusing, particularly at finer resolutions. To address these issues, we propose a shadow-aided 2-D sparse Bayesian autofocusing method for high-resolution imaging of MTs in THz circular SAR (CSAR). First, a CSAR echo model for MTs is derived, and 2-D velocity estimation is achieved by exploiting shadow information, which enables initial motion compensation. Second, considering that MTs typically exist only in specific regions of the scene and comprise a limited number of strong scatterers, indicating considerable sparsity, a 2-D autofocusing sparse Bayesian model is established by reconstructing the region-of-interest (ROI) echo after motion compensation. Finally, under a hierarchical Laplacian prior, refined GMTIm is realized by minimizing the image entropy (IE) of the range and azimuth signals, respectively. The proposed framework can adaptively handle unknown phase errors and significantly improve imaging quality. Simulations verify the accuracy of the 2-D velocity estimation and the resulting focusing improvement. Field experiments (with no accurate reference target velocities available) further demonstrate the imaging and autofocusing performance of the proposed method.
author: Xiaoyu Qin, Yang Zeng, Hongqiang Wang, Mingyao Chen, Bin Deng

title: Collaborative Cross-Modal Fusion With Dynamic Enhancement and Reconstruction Guidance for UAV Object Detection
content: Cross-modal fusion detection utilizing visible (RGB) and infrared (IR) images has emerged as a promising solution for uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) perception, especially in complex or low-light environments. To alleviate the adverse effects of residual cross-modal feature misalignment, enhance multiscale representation, and reduce the computational overhead of fusion, this article proposes a novel collaboration cross-modal fusion (CCMFusion) framework that integrates three key components. Specifically, the dual-domain enhancement (DDE) module employs separate enhancement branches to improve feature discriminability along the channel and spatial dimensions, respectively, thereby highlighting object features while effectively suppressing background noise. The cross-modal interaction fusion (CIF) module integrates spatially aligned gated interaction (SAGI) and frequency-aligned guidance methods to align and exchange complementary information across different modalities, thereby capturing modality-specific cues and bridging semantic gaps. The cross-reconstruction and fusion (CRF) module further refines fused features via a reconstruction-based learning paradigm, combining a cross-modal guided reconstruction loss to preserve both shared and unique characteristics with a frequency-aware pooling strategy for global–local context integration. Extensive experiments on the DroneVehicle and FLIR datasets demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance, with an  $mAP_{50}$  of 82.9% and an  $mAP$  of 56.8% on the DroneVehicle, and an  $mAP_{50}$  of 80.9% and an  $mAP$  of 45.8% on the FLIR, significantly surpassing all compared approaches. The proposed framework provides a promising foundation for multimodal UAV perception and lays a solid foundation for future research, while practical edge deployment still requires further lightweight optimization. https://github.com/Caifei123/
author: Fei Cai, Zhong Qu, Xuehui Yin, Yuhong Pan

title: Physics-Constrained Dual-Prototype Learning Network for Few-Shot Class-Incremental Hyperspectral Image Classification
content: Few-shot class-incremental learning (FSCIL) in hyperspectral image classification (HSIC) is challenging because the model can only access a few labeled samples from novel classes, while these novel classes may be spectrally similar to old classes despite belonging to different categories. When the base stage also contains few labeled samples, old-class prototypes may already be biased due to insufficient supervision. As similar novel classes are continuously introduced, such bias can accumulate and make old prototypes unreliable anchors, misleading novel prototype construction and blurring decision boundaries. However, existing methods mainly rely on feature similarity for prototype calibration or knowledge transfer, which may ignore physical relevance and introduce unreliable old-class information. Moreover, the old-class prototype structure may degrade during incremental learning, further aggravating old-class forgetting. To address these problems, this article proposes a physics-constrained dual-prototype learning network for few-shot class-incremental HSIC. First, a physics-constrained Mamba network is constructed to extract physically consistent features, and feature prototypes and physical prototypes are built for classification and physical relevance modeling. Second, a prototype structure distillation (PSD) module preserves old-class prototype relations to alleviate forgetting and local boundary degradation. Furthermore, a physics-guided prototype calibration (PGPC) mechanism is designed to calibrate novel prototypes according to physical relevance derived from physical prototypes, while maintaining sufficient margins between physically related old and novel classes. Experiments on three HSI datasets show that the proposed method outperforms representative FSCIL methods, demonstrating its effectiveness and stability.
author: Chen Ding, Sirui Zheng, Pengfei Wan, Canyu Zhang, Yizhuo Dong, Wenqiang Hua, Song Yan, Lei Zhang, Wei Wei

title: Open-Set Domain Adaptation for Hyperspectral Image Classification via Adaptive Class-Aware Boundaries and Preserving Semantic Structure
content: In hyperspectral image (HSI) classification, domain adaptation techniques aim to address the scarcity of labeled data in the target scene. However, in practice, the target scene often contains land cover classes unseen in the source domain. This open-set setting introduces two core challenges: first, unknown classes in the target domain are prone to misclassification; second, forcibly aligning the entire target domain, including unknown classes, with the source domain not only leads to “negative transfer” due to interference from these unknown classes but also corrupts the intrinsic semantic structure of the target domain data. To tackle this challenge, this article proposes an open-set domain adaptation (OSDA) framework with a dynamic adaptive class-aware boundary (DACB) and target-domain semantic structure preservation (TSSP). The framework accurately identifies unknown class samples by dynamically learning an adaptive boundary for each known class and uses this boundary information to guide a weighted alignment, adapting only high-confidence known classes to mitigate negative transfer. Simultaneously, an entropy-driven self-supervised TSSP module minimizes the entropy of a joint neighborhood–prototype assignment distribution to strengthen high-similarity relations and suppress low-similarity relations. It further uses a prediction-entropy-based separation (ES) objective to repel potential unknown samples from known-class decision regions, thereby preserving the intrinsic semantic structure of the target domain and improving feature discriminability. Superior performance across multiple tasks and openness experiments on six different datasets demonstrates the proposed method’s effectiveness and robustness. The code is available at https://github.com/Li-ZK/ACBS-2026
author: Mingtai Qi, Zhaokui Li, Yushi Chen, Wei Li, Xuewei Gong, Jing Tian, Jinjun Wang, Qian Du

title: Real-Time Hardware Acceleration of Recursive Simplex Growing Algorithm for Finding Endmembers in Hyperspectral Imagery
content: Simplex volume (SV) is a widely used criterion which satisfies both abundance sum-to-one constraint (ASC) and abundance non-negativity constraint (ANC) for fully abundance constrained spectral unmixing (SU). It has been also used to develop endmember finding (EF) algorithms such as simplex growing algorithm (SGA). The main issue arising in SGA is its excessive computational complexity resulting from finding the determinant in SV calculation (SVC). To resolve this issue, orthogonal projection (OP)-based SGA (OPSGA) and geometric SGA (GSGA) are developed to remove the necessity of finding determinant. However, these two algorithms still require  $O(L^{3})$  computational complexity with  $L$  being the total number of bands. To further improve their computational complexity, an algorithm called recursive SGA (R-SGA) is developed to reduce the complexity from  $O(L^{3})$  to  $O(L^{2})$  in both data processing and storage memory. Moreover, a hardware architecture for R-SGA is physically implemented onto a field-programmable gate array (FPGA), which further divides the overall  $O(L^{2})$  complexity into  $O(L)$  resource complexity and  $O(L)$  time complexity, making it the simplest, most efficient, and most performant hardware accelerated architecture to date for SGA. The hardware architecture is tested and validated by experiments performed on real hyperspectral image scenes, and fully characterized in terms of efficiency and performance for real-time applications.
author: Minh Quan P. Tran, Lin Wang, Chein-I. Chang

title: SAM-Guided Region-Aware Spectral–Spatial Learning Framework for Hyperspectral Image Classification With Limited Samples
content: Hyperspectral image (HSI) classification with limited training samples remains challenging because sparse annotations provide insufficient supervision for learning reliable spectral–spatial representations. Existing label-efficient methods mainly exploit spectral and spatial information within the HSI, while region-level structural cues are often underused. To address this limitation, we propose SRSSNet, a segment anything model (SAM)-guided region-aware spectral–spatial learning framework for HSI classification with limited samples. SRSSNet first generates candidate region masks from HSI-derived visual representations using the SAM and refines them to construct a structurally coherent region prior map. The region prior map is then incorporated into a dual-branch network to guide spatial and spectral feature learning. In the spatial branch, a region-guided Transformer modulation (RGTM) module is proposed to aggregate region-aware tokens, perform contextual reasoning among regions, and use the enhanced tokens to modulate spatial features. In the spectral branch, a region-conditioned spectral calibration (RCSC) module is introduced to derive intraregion spectral statistics and calibrate pixelwise spectral embeddings through a gated residual mechanism. The features from the two branches are subsequently fused for classification. Experiments on three public HSI benchmarks under limited-sample settings demonstrate that SRSSNet achieves favorable performance compared with representative state-of-the-art methods. The code will be made available at https://github.com/YueLi-lab/SRSSNet
author: Yue Li, Mengjiao Tang, Yu Shen, Liang Xiao, Qian Du

title: AeroFuse: A Robust and Lightweight HSI–LiDAR Fusion Framework for Onboard Remote Sensing
content: Artificial intelligence and onboard computing are moving remote sensing from the traditional “acquire-then-downlink” mode toward real-time interpretation directly on airborne platforms. Since the joint data volume of hyperspectral imagery (HSI) and light detection and ranging (LiDAR) often exceeds the downlink budget, HSI–LiDAR fusion is increasingly expected to run onboard. Onboard fusion, however, faces three practical issues: spectral degradation caused by noise and radiometric disturbances, cross-modal spatial misalignment, and tight limits on computation, power, and latency. We present AeroFuse, a robust and lightweight fusion framework that handles each issue with a dedicated design. A geometry-anchored spectral encoder (Anchor-Enc) uses the stable LiDAR-derived geometry as a structural reference to stabilize degraded spectral features. A bidirectional bridge attention module (Bidirectional Bridge-Attn) with gated residual fusion builds feature-level cross-modal correspondence without an explicit registration module, improving tolerance to moderate spatial offsets. LiDAR Tokenization compresses the LiDAR stream into a few tokens to bound the cost of cross-modal interaction, and a lightweight conformer-based classifier operates on the resulting compact token set. Experiments on five HSI–LiDAR/DSM benchmarks (Houston, Trento, MUUFL, Houston2018, and Augsburg) show that AeroFuse achieves accuracy competitive with or better than recent fusion networks, e.g., 93.13% overall accuracy (OA) on Houston, with about 0.7 M parameters and 0.1 GFLOPs per forward pass. Additional evaluations further verify its generalization across different airborne sensing conditions. Deployment tests on an embedded NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin module demonstrate the efficiency of AeroFuse for onboard HSI–LiDAR interpretation.
author: Siyuan Wan, Jiuniu Wang, Mugen Peng, Yuanben Zhang, Wenjia Xu

title: Vocabulary Lock-In in Remote-Sensing Open-Vocabulary Detectors for Cross-Taxonomy Disaster Damage Assessment
content: Rapid building-damage mapping from satellite and aerial imagery supports disaster response. Yet disaster-management agencies often use different taxonomies for comparable damage, so a closed-vocabulary detector must be retrained for each taxonomy. Open-vocabulary detectors (OVDs) accept textual class prompts and could adapt through prompt changes alone. Their performance on overhead remote-sensing imagery is insufficient without domain-specific fine-tuning, so practitioners fine-tune first and expect the prompt flexibility to carry over. This article identifies a previously uncharacterized failure mode in remote-sensing imagery processing: vocabulary lock-in, in which a fine-tuned detector loses access to a learned damage class when its training label is replaced by a semantically equivalent synonym. To explain this failure, we propose a diagnostic framework that asks in sequence how much lock-in occurs, when it develops during fine-tuning, and where it resides within the model. On a five-dataset disaster building-damage benchmark, a matched-granularity cross-taxonomy vocabulary substitution on FloodNet produces a mean 26.5% mean average precision (mAP)@50 drop, present in all five seeds. Of this drop, 16.3% is already present in the pretrained detector and 10.2% is attributable to fine-tuning. The same-domain direct-synonym substitution on the xBD test set, with images, annotations, taxonomy, and weights fixed, yields at least as large a relative drop. On Grounding DETR with improved denoising anchor boxes (DINO), training dynamics show that lock-in develops progressively during fine-tuning, while parameter-partition freezing localizes it to the grounding side. Strong weight-space constraints leave novel-vocabulary access unchanged, while direct decoder-attention measurements reveal prompt-dependent allocation under fixed weights. Our analysis therefore points to an activation-level access problem rather than weight drift. Based on this analysis, we introduce Embedding Bridge, a training-free method that expresses each unfamiliar class-name embedding as a weighted combination of familiar training-name embeddings. It restores access without changing model weights. It improves Grounding DINO on three of the four cross-taxonomy targets: by 6.8% mAP on FloodNet, 4.7% on RescueNet, and 1.7% on extensible building damage (EBD).
author: Zhipeng Liu, Chunbo Luo, Wei Han, Christos Grecos

title: BSGA: Bitemporal Semantic Gated Adapter for Remote Sensing Change Detection
content: Visual foundation models (VFMs) have substantially improved remote sensing change detection (CD). Existing VFM-based CD methods mainly improve task-specific adaptation and bitemporal interaction from different perspectives. However, the reliability of bitemporal difference discrimination under cross-temporal semantic inconsistency, caused by appearance variations, remains insufficiently explored. To address this limitation, we propose the bitemporal semantic gated adapter (BSGA), a plug-in module that strengthens explicit bitemporal difference modeling and improves VFM-based CD. In particular, BSGA incorporates a prototype-guided semantic alignment (PGSA) module to enhance cross-temporal semantic consistency. The PGSA reconstructs semantic features for bitemporal remote sensing images with a shared set of learnable semantic prototypes. In addition, BSGA introduces a difference-semantic interaction gating (DSIG) module for feature modulation to highlight true changes while suppressing pseudochanges. The DSIG uses the feature difference between bitemporal images as a prior and combines it with reconstructed semantic contexts to guide the modulation process. Experiments on three public datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and advantages of BSGA for remote sensing CD. Moreover, BSGA can be seamlessly integrated into diverse VFMs, including DINOv3 and SAM2, to further improve CD performance.
author: Fei Tong, Dou Quan, Ning Huyan, Pei He, Shuang Wang, Yunan Li, Licheng Jiao

title: TKA-WSCD: Integrating Text Prompts With Self-Distillation and Cross-Modal Feature Alignment for Weakly Supervised Remote Sensing Change Detection
content: Remote sensing image change detection (CD) is essential for Earth observation and spatiotemporal analysis. However, fully supervised methods require extensive pixel-level annotations, limiting practicality and motivating weakly supervised approaches. A key challenge is that image-level labels provide limited prior information, making it difficult to accurately localize pixel-level changes. Vision–language foundation models offer a promising solution. Therefore, we propose TKA-weakly supervised CD (WSCD), a novel weakly supervised change detection framework that integrates text prompts with self-distillation and cross-modal feature alignment. TKA-WSCD extracts visual difference features from bi-temporal images via self-distillation and aligns them with textual descriptions based on a vision–language foundation model to improve accuracy. Specifically, we propose a DINOv3-based teacher–student bi-temporal self-distillation encoder, where the teacher network guides the student network via different fusion strategies to learn generalizable and robust visual representations of changed regions. Second, cross-modal alignment between textual descriptions and visual information is proposed to map textual and visual features of changed areas into a semantically consistent joint embedding space, generating alignment features that guide visual features to better discriminate changed areas. Finally, a text-guided cross-modal multitask objective function is designed, in which image-level classification, visual feature-consistency representations of the self-distillation network, and vision–text cross-modal alignment pixel-level segmentation are jointly optimized to achieve accurate change localization. Experimental results on WHU-CDC and LEVIR-CDC show TKA-WSCD obtains  $F1$ -scores of 80.71% and 76.39%, outperforming mainstream weakly supervised methods and possessing prominent advantages in improving changed region integrity and accuracy under complex remote sensing scenes. The code is available at https://github.com/ZhangAilan/TKA-WSCD
author: Yuehao Zhang, Nan Mo, Gege Ma, Gaozhe Li

title: A Physically Consistent End-to-End Framework for Modeling and Imaging of Time-Varying Infrared Signatures of Space Targets
content: Infrared (IR) signature analysis of space targets is essential for space situational awareness (SSA), enabling reliable detection, identification, and characterization of objects in orbit. However, existing studies often address IR radiation modeling or imaging simulation separately, lacking a unified framework that consistently links the external thermal environment, target thermal response, IR radiation, and image formation. In this study, an end-to-end imaging framework is proposed for high-fidelity IR signature simulation of space targets. The framework integrates space external heat-flux modeling, thermal response simulation, effective IR radiation calculation, and IR image formation within a unified pipeline. Multiple radiation sources, including solar radiation, Earth thermal emission, and Earth albedo, are considered, while the influences of Earth’s underlying surface and atmospheric environment are incorporated to improve environmental realism. To validate the coupled thermal-response and IR-radiation prediction components of the proposed framework, a ground-based thermal-vacuum experiment is conducted under controlled conditions. A low-temperature environment representative of deep space is established, and combined directional heat fluxes are applied to emulate solar and Earth radiation. IR measurements in long-wave bands are acquired and compared with simulation results. The comparison demonstrates good agreement in both temporal evolution and radiative magnitude, validating the coupled radiative–thermal prediction under the prescribed boundary conditions.
author: Qianwen Wang, Ruoxi Peng, Biao Zhang

title: 3-D Parallel Inversion of Controlled-Source Electromagnetic Data Using Dual Unstructured Meshes
content: 3-D numerical inversion of controlled-source electromagnetic (CSEM) data is the current trend for geophysical prospecting. In this article, we propose a 3-D parallel inversion approach for CSEM data based on dual unstructured meshes. The forward modeling is employed using an unstructured finite element method, while the inversion problem is solved using the computationally efficient limited-memory Broyden–Fletcher–Goldfarb–Shanno (L-BFGS) method, which employs the reciprocity theorem to compute the sensitivity. This article adopts dual unstructured meshes for forward and inverse modeling separately. The inversion mesh is used for discretizing model parameters. The forward mesh is locally refined from the inversion mesh based on frequency, field source, receiver positions, and the distance between elements and these points. This dual-mesh strategy reduces singularities at source positions and improves modeling accuracy at receiver positions without increasing the number of inversion parameters, thereby enhancing the inversion efficiency and flexibility of CSEM data with multisources and multifrequencies. Subsequently, a message passing interface (MPI)-based parallel strategy is implemented to enhance computational efficiency. The convergence and reliability of the proposed algorithm are validated through single anomaly model, basin model, and complex model cases. It is further applied to field data in Karamay region in Xinjiang, China, to test its applicability. Results demonstrate that the algorithm exhibits a certain degree of noise resistance and good reliability, further validating its practicality and robustness.
author: Yixin Ye, Ruodan Yang, Zhixin Liu, Shengping Gong, Chaofeng Wu

title: Seismic Blind Deconvolution Based on Nested EM–SMC Algorithm
content: Seismic blind deconvolution is an ill-posed problem due to the unknown source wavelet and reflectivity sequence. In this work, we propose a nested blind deconvolution method, which combines both the expectation–maximization (EM) and sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) methods for simultaneous estimation of both the wavelet and reflectivity sequence. In the proposed work, we initially assume priors for the wavelet, reflectivity sequence, and noise. The EM method estimates hyperparameters of the assumed priors. Meanwhile, SMC estimates the posterior distributions by leveraging the prior distributions within a Bayesian inference method. The proposed method is applied to synthetic, field, and well-log datasets for deconvolution. Quantitative metrics like signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), mean-square error (mse), and structural similarity index measure (SSIM) are used to evaluate the proposed method. The results indicate that the proposed method accurately estimates the wavelet and reflectivity sequence when applied to synthetic datasets, field datasets, and well-log datasets.
author: Dokku Tejaswi, Nakka Shekhar, Anup Kumar Mandpura, Sunil Chinnadurai, Karthikeyan Elumalai

title: Viscoacoustic Least-Squares Reverse-Time Migration Using Wasserstein-2 Distance Objective Function
content: Least-squares reverse-time migration (LSRTM) has become an advanced technology for imaging complex subsurface structures because it can provide a migration image with higher resolution and more balanced amplitude than conventional reverse-time migration (RTM). However, the absorption and attenuation characteristics of the subsurface media will lead to amplitude attenuation and phase dispersion of the seismic wavefield, resulting in an inaccurate reflectivity profile obtained by LSRTM. In addition, since LSRTM is a linear inversion method based on the weak scattering assumption, its migration imaging results usually have high background model dependence. The traditional LSRTM is based on the  $L_{2}$  norm as the objective function. When the background model is poor, the inverted result is easy to fall into a local minimum. To alleviate these issues, we propose a data-domain viscoacoustic LSRTM ( $Q$ LSRTM) algorithm based on the 1-D Wasserstein-2 ( $W_{2}$ ) distance objective function. In particular, we use the decoupled constant- $Q$  fractional Laplace viscoacoustic wave equation to describe the attenuation effect of the subsurface, and reduce the dependence of the LSRTM on the background model by using the  $W_{2}$  distance objective function with better convexity. Since the  $W_{2}$  distance in the optimal transport (OT) theory has better convexity than the  $L_{2}$  norm, it can better avoid the inversion falling into a local minimum. In this article, we perform nonnegative normalization preprocessing on seismic data to meet the requirements of the OT distance for data. We verify the effectiveness and practicality of the proposed strategy by numerical tests of synthetic and field data. The migration results show that even in the case of a poor background model,  $W_{2}$ -based  $Q$ LSRTM can effectively compensate for the attenuation effect, improve the resolution, and suppress the migration artifacts in the inverted reflectivity profile.
author: Jihang Han, Hui Zhou, Mingkun Zhang, Hanming Chen, Lingqian Wang

author: Yanfei Ma, Tongren Xu, Shaomin Liu, Ziwei Xu

title: AECNet: A Lightweight Change Detection Network Combining Cross-Scale and Antisymmetric Differential Feature Modeling
content: Remote sensing change detection (RSCD) is critical for analyzing surface change based on Earth observations. In recent years, the accuracy of RSCD has been improved with the application of deep learning technologies. High-performance change detection (CD) models often achieve superior accuracy at the cost of substantial model complexity and computational overhead. In contrast, lightweight architectures remain prone to false detections in subtle change regions and often fail to sufficiently capture deep cross-temporal dependencies. This study proposes AECNet, a lightweight and efficient CD network that could address these challenges through three functionally complementary modules integrated into a hierarchical pipeline. First, the cross-scale aggregation module can enhance multigranularity feature representations within each temporal branch through dual-path downsampling and cross-scale fusion. Second, the antisymmetric differential feature enhancement can enable differentiated perception of change signals across varying magnitudes by decomposing the difference representation into strong and weak components. Third, the efficient cross-temporal mining can capture deep temporal dependencies through lightweight feature interaction and adaptive attention fusion. Extensive experiments on LEVIR-CD, WHU-CD, and SYSU-CD demonstrate that AECNet, with only 3.76 M parameters, achieves state-of-the-art detection performance relative to other methods, attaining F1 scores of 91.51%, 93.85%, and 83.78%, respectively. The AECNet proposed also presents promising potential for extension to more complex scenarios, such as forest CD, due to the capabilities of strong–weak change decomposition and cross-temporal modeling.
author: Rumeng Wang, Shilin Zou, Shaoyu Zhang, Xiaohui Zha, Rong Liu, Duan Huang

title: RCFNet: Reliability-Aware Optical–SAR Fusion for Cloud-Robust Surface Water Extraction From Sentinel-1/2 Imagery
content: Hydrological monitoring is a fundamental pillar of environmental governance; however, accurate surface water extraction from satellite imagery remains challenging due to cloud interference, shadow-induced spectral confusion, and background complexity. To address these challenges, this study constructs a manually annotated multisource Sentinel-1/2 water body dataset for a cloud-prone region in the upper Yangtze River basin and proposes the reliability-aware cross-modal fusion network (RCFNet). Specifically, RCFNet introduces a cross-modal reliability gate to estimate the relative reliability of optical and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) information by jointly considering modality-specific features, cross-modal context, and feature discrepancies. This allows the network to adaptively adjust the contribution of the two modalities before deeper feature extraction. A hybrid convolutional neural network–Swin transformer encoder is then used to preserve local boundary details while capturing broader spatial context, followed by efficient multiscale attention for multiscale spatial refinement and a squeeze-and-excitation block for channel recalibration. These components operate at different stages of the network and together form a coordinated multimodal processing framework. Controlled pseudocloud experiments further show that SAR provides increasingly important complementary information as optical observations deteriorate, while the SAR-induced gain exhibits different stages of change. Similar transition patterns were also observed in several representative architectures, suggesting that the benefit of optical–SAR fusion depends on the changing quality and complementarity of the two sensing modalities. Overall, RCFNet provides an effective all-weather framework for water-body mapping in complex terrain.
author: Rui Liu, Dongchen Yao, Bilian Zhuo, Qi Zhou, Shihui Wu

title: FG-ConvLSTM: A Physics-Informed Deep Learning Framework for Ocean Frontal-Zone Intensity Prediction With Frontal-Line-Guided Attention
content: Ocean fronts are highly productive regions that play a crucial role in marine ecosystems. The dynamic evolution of their location and intensity is of great importance for fishery resource assessment, disaster prevention, and marine environmental monitoring.. However, ocean-front evolution is driven by the coupling of multiple dynamical processes and therefore exhibits strong spatiotemporal nonlinearity. Moreover, frontal zones are extremely sparse in large-scale sea surface temperature (SST) images. As a result, conventional data-driven models tend to overlook narrow frontal bands during forecasting and suffer from an oversmoothing problem, leading to blurred frontal boundaries, weakened local high-gradient structures, and limited capability in capturing subtle changes in frontal position and intensity. To address these challenges, this article focuses on ocean thermal-front intensity prediction and proposes a physics-informed deep learning forecasting framework, termed FG-ConvLSTM. The proposed framework consists of three key components. First, a multiscale initial feature extraction module is introduced to capture both fine-grained details and large-scale spatial structures in the SST field. Second, a frontal-line-guided dual attention mechanism is developed, in which the observed frontal-line locations are explicitly incorporated as physical prior knowledge into both spatial and channel attention calculations, thereby guiding the model to focus on high-gradient frontal boundaries. Third, a frontal-zone-weighted loss function is designed by assigning a 50-fold error penalty to pixels within the observed frontal zones, effectively alleviating the imbalance caused by the dominance of nonfrontal background regions. The study region west of Luzon Island contains a seasonally evolving thermal-front system that is generally more pronounced during boreal winter but undergoes substantial changes in position, extent, and intensity throughout the year. Its wintertime development has been linked primarily to the encounter between a northward warm tongue generated by geostrophic thermal advection and colder surrounding water, making this region a challenging test area for year-round frontal-zone intensity prediction. Experiments covering the full annual cycle in the seasonally evolving thermal-front region west of Luzon Island in the South China Sea demonstrate that FG-ConvLSTM achieves superior performance in short-term (1-D), medium-term (3-D), and long-term (7-D) prediction tasks. The proposed model better preserves the continuity and sharpness of frontal structures and shows stronger capability in frontal-zone intensity characterization and spatial-detail reconstruction. In terms of key metrics, including tolerance-based accuracy Acc@0.1 (±0.018 °C/km) and the coefficient of determination within frontal zones, denoted as frontal-zone R2, FG-ConvLSTM consistently and substantially outperforms mainstream spatiotemporal baseline models, including long short-term memory, ConvLSTM, ConvGRU and Attention-ConvNet. This study improves the accuracy of frontal-zone intensity prediction under complex oceanic backgrounds and provides a new solution for high-resolution forecasting of mesoscale ocean dynamical phenomena.
author: Zhilin He, Ruili Sun, Yanzhen Gu, Peiliang Li, Hui Huang

title: Typhoon Center Fix Using an Adaptive Core Region Discrimination From CYGNSS Wind Speed
content: Spaceborne global navigation satellite system-reflectometry (GNSS-R) provides sea surface wind speeds, but the irregular ground tracks of its specular points often lead to incomplete spatial coverage of a typhoon region within short time windows. Moreover, the lack of reliable low-wind retrievals in the eye region and the absence of wind direction information render conventional center-fixing methods—based on calm-eye identification or cyclonic circulation analysis—inapplicable to GNSS-R data. This study develops a typhoon center fixing method that relies solely on the spatiotemporal distribution of wind speed magnitudes within a 3-h time window. First, the raw irregular observations are gridded while accounting for their sampling times and the spatial correlation structure. Then, an adaptive wind speed threshold and connected component analysis are employed to discriminate the core region of the typhoon from the gridded cyclone global navigation satellite system wind speeds and obtain an initial center estimate. Finally, the initial center is refined by leveraging the more stable wind speed profile in the outer region and the observation coverage in each sector. According to the availability criteria, usable observation windows are separated by approximately 9 h on average; for cases with sufficient coverage, the mean center-fixing distance error is approximately 50 km. Sensitivity analysis reveals that center-fixing accuracy improves with denser observation coverage and with observations closer to the typhoon center, and that it also increases with typhoon intensity and decreasing radius of maximum wind. Overall, GNSS-R demonstrates significant potential for typhoon center fixing.
author: Xiangchao Ma, Dongkai Yang, Feng Wang, Weichen Sun, Chuanrui Tan, Mengjie Wang, Honglin Li

title: A Deep Neural Network-Gridded Model for PWV Adjustment in GNSS Remote Sensing
content: Precipitable water vapor (PWV) is a key factor in extreme weather, water cycle, and surface temperature regulation, but the elevation differences of multisource observation data make it necessary to perform vertical calculations when used together. Traditional water vapor vertical adjustment models are difficult to accurately capture the complex nonlinear variation characteristics of PWV in the vertical direction. To make up for this deficiency, this study, based on deep neural networks and using European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts reanalysis (ERA5) PWV from 2016 to 2018, constructed three gridded PWV vertical adjustment models (B-PWVC1, B-PWVC2, and B-PWVC5) in China and its surrounding areas, and compared them with the latest C-PWVC1 model. The results show that the B-PWVC1 model, with a spatial resolution of 1° × 1°, achieves higher accuracy and better stability than the other models. When the ERA5 PWV is vertically corrected with the global navigation satellite system PWV in 2019 as a reference, the root-mean-square error of B-PWVC1, B-PWVC2, and B-PWVC5 models proposed in this study decreased by 13.09%, 12.69%, and 12.69% against the C-PWVC1 model, respectively. Temporal analysis based on monthly error statistics further demonstrates the stability of the B-PWVC models. No significant degradation is observed during the high-moisture summer months. In addition, the B-PWVC1, B-PWVC2, and B-PWVC5 models still performed stably during the Chaba typhoon event, with improvements of 39.74%, 35.39%, and 31.13% for PWV vertical adjustment compared with the C-PWVC1 model, respectively. The results indicate that the models developed in this study effectively capture the vertical variation characteristics of PWV and have potential application for extreme weather monitoring.
author: Liangke Huang, Haoyun Pang, Peng Yuan, Junyu Li, Shaofeng Xie, Lilong Liu

title: Multilevel Cross-Temporal Interaction Mamba for Hyperspectral Multiclass Change Detection
content: Multiclass change detection (MCD) in hyperspectral images often encounters challenges, such as missed and false detections, due to the uneven distribution of samples across categories. In addition, categories with fewer samples may even be undetectable or exhibit the poor detection performance. To address this issue, this study proposes a multilevel cross-temporal interaction Mamba for hyperspectral MCD. We design a full information feature extraction Mamba module that effectively captures local and global, spatial, and spectral information from images. This allows the model to maintain the overall semantic context. Enhanced detection of irregular and small change areas, reducing false positives and false negatives. In addition, a cross-temporal Mamba module was introduced to exchange Mamba's dual temporal learnable parameters, which facilitates cross-temporal feature alignment and deep fusion, making semantic differences between dual temporal images more pronounced. Furthermore, a binary change map prior pregenerated by the spectral frequency-induced edge enhancement transformer is introduced to guide the network toward potential change regions. By enhancing both changed and unchanged features, the proposed method improves the discrimination of change boundaries and reduces false and missed detections. The MCD method achieves favorable overall accuracy and average accuracy on four publicly available datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness in improving MCD performance while reducing missed detections and false alarms.
author: Xiaobing Yu, Shibo Sun, Jiaqiang Qi, Le Sun, Yang Xu, Tianming Zhan

title: Effective Classification of Marine Features by Fusion of SAR Imagery and Meteo-Marine Data
content: This manuscript examines the integration of meteo-marine information in the classification of sea surface phenomena in synthetic aperture radar data. A simple deep learning framework is used to evaluate how data fusion can improve the interpretability of otherwise ambiguous scenes. The SAR images are sourced from the TenGeoP-SARwv dataset, excluding ice-related classes. Spatially and temporally coregistered meteo-marine data, such as wind speed and surface temperature, are extracted from the ERA5 and Copernicus marine environment monitoring service datasets. A modular convolutional neural network is employed, with separate branches for image and meteo-marine data that are fused before classification. Across three training seeds, the full-grid multimodal model achieves an accuracy of $0.845 \pm 0.023$, compared with $0.801 \pm 0.010$ for the image-only model, corresponding to an average absolute gain of 4.45 percentage points. Performance gains are especially notable for classes influenced by atmospheric or oceanographic conditions, such as wind streaks and oceanic fronts. Explainability methods, including integrated gradients and saliency maps, are applied to selected case studies to analyze the contribution of each data modality and highlight how environmental context aids in disambiguating visually similar patterns. The results therefore support contextual fusion as a means of improving overall accuracy, while showing that its effects are class- and sample-dependent.
author: Angela Carmen Cristofano, Andrea Mazzeo, Paolo Vavasori, Alfredo Renga, Maria Daniela Graziano

title: SUnG-Soil: Unmixing-Guided Representations for Spaceborne Hyperspectral Soil Property Retrieval
content: Hyperspectral soil mapping in agricultural landscapes is often constrained by mixed pixels, where vegetation, residues, and shadow weaken soil-related spectral signals. This study investigates whether physics-informed deep spectral unmixing can improve soil property prediction by transforming mixed spaceborne hyperspectral observations into soil-aware representations. Using Tanager-1 imagery and field-measured endmembers from two agricultural sites in Northern Greece, representing a vineyard scale case and a broader regional scale case, we compare raw spectral reflectance with two unmixing-guided representations: a physically constrained orthogonal subspace projection that suppresses nonsoil components and a learned latent embedding derived from a spatial–spectral autoencoder trained under a linear mixing constraint. Results indicate that the best representation depends on scale and scene complexity. In the vineyard site, the projection-based approach yields the highest mean performance for soil organic carbon (SOC), clay, and pH, while at the more heterogeneous regional site, the learned embedding performs best across all targets. Using image-derived components as endmembers generally weakened predictive performance and produced less consistent gains over raw reflectance. Vegetation-sensitivity analysis further suggests that both weaken the association between vegetation fraction and prediction error, particularly for SOC. Overall, the study shows that spectral unmixing can support spaceborne hyperspectral soil retrieval not only as a preprocessing step, but also as a mechanism for designing physically informed representations under mixed-pixel conditions.
author: Haris Ampas, Konstantinos Karyotis, Pierre Guillevic, George Zalidis, Sophia Petridou

title: Shared-Pattern Collaborative Network for Multisource Remote Sensing Data Classification
content: Multisource remote sensing data classification has received growing attention recently. However, existing methods still struggle to jointly model long-range contextual dependencies and shared spatial patterns across heterogeneous modalities. To address this issue, we propose a shared-pattern collaborative network (SPCNet) for HSI and SAR/LiDAR joint classification. To enhance cross-modal collaborative learning, shared-pattern collaborative block is designed by introducing a shared large-kernel operator and a dynamic convolution branch, enabling the network to capture common spatial structures and content-adaptive local features. Furthermore, region-adaptive modality allocator is developed to assign spatially varying modality weights for reliable feature fusion. Experiments on Houston2013, Augsburg, and Houston2018 datasets demonstrate that SPCNet achieves superior classification performance over several state-of-the-art methods.
author: Chenfang Yang, Chuanzheng Gong, Feng Gao, Junyu Dong, Qian Du

title: Analysis of Time Series of L-Band SAR Copol and Cross-Pol Phase Difference Related to Crop Structure
content: Accurate monitoring of crop phenology and canopy structure is essential for agricultural growth monitoring and yield estimation. Polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (SAR) is sensitive to canopy structure, yet the physical mechanisms linking polarization phase differences to crop properties remain insufficiently explored. This study introduces the equivalent scattering phase center (ESPC) framework to interpret polarimetric phase differences by relating the vertical separation of scattering centers under different polarizations to measurable phase difference values. Using L-band uninhabited aerial vehicle synthetic aperture radar data acquired over Winnipeg, Canada, during the soil moisture active passive validation experiment 2012 campaign, we analyze the temporal evolution of copolarization phase difference (CPD) and cross-polarization phase difference (XPD) for eight crop types (canola, corn, beans, pasture, wheat, winter wheat, oats, and forage) throughout their growing seasons. Results show that CPD tracks phenological development, with canola exhibiting a sign reversal corresponding to the transition from leaf-dominated to stem-dominated scattering and corn maintaining persistently negative values consistent with its vertical stalk architecture. Spatial distribution maps reveal regular spatial patterns and progressive canopy homogenization. Correlation analysis with in situ biophysical measurements demonstrates strong CPD relationships with dry biomass for forage ($R = -0.96$), corn ($R = -0.86$), oats ($R = 0.81$), and canola ($R = -0.75$) at their respective optimal incidence angle classes, while the XPD of beans reaches $|R| = 0.89$ with crop height. Incidence angle stratification proves critical, as the CPD correlations for corn reach $|R| = 0.86$ at medium angles but fall below $|R| = 0.25$ at high angles. Polarimetric coherence provides complementary sensitivity ($|R|$ up to 0.86), particularly at shallow incidence angles where phase difference correlations weaken. These findings demonstrate that polarization phase differences, interpreted through the ESPC framework and stratified by incidence angle, offer a physically grounded approach for quantitative crop structure monitoring with quad-polarization SAR.
author: Hongtao Shi, Qing Wu, Juan M. Lopez-Sanchez, Zhong Lu, Tianjie Zhao

title: Optical-Semantic Guidance and Graph-Structure Enhancement for Few-Shot SAR Segmentation
content: Compared with optical remote-sensing imaging, synthetic aperture radar (SAR) offers distinct advantages under adverse weather conditions and in complex battlefield environments. However, feature optimization and segmentation of SAR imagery have long remained challenging, owing to the presence of coherent speckle noise and the intrinsic scarcity of visual semantic cues. These limitations are particularly pronounced in data-scarce regimes, where existing deep models struggle to escape their reliance on large-scale annotated datasets. As a consequence, segmentation outputs in SAR scenes often fail to provide reliable semantic support for downstream target recognition. To address these challenges, we propose an optical-semantics guided and graph-structure enhanced network (OSG-GSE), designed to advance few-shot learning performance for SAR imagery from both local structural and global semantic perspectives. At the structural level, we construct topological graphs from optical images to derive high-level representations encoding land-cover adjacency relationships. Through a cross-modal structural injection module, these topological priors are transferred to SAR features, enhancing geometric discriminability without compromising intrinsic scattering characteristics. At the semantic level, we introduce a nonlinear prototype mapping from optical to SAR domains, enabling recalibration of class centroids derived from few-shot SAR support samples. This strategy mitigates prototype drift induced by coherent speckle noise and outlier samples. Extensive experiments on publicly available datasets demonstrate that the proposed optical-guided SAR segmentation framework substantially outperforms existing unimodal segmentation baselines under few-shot settings. These results substantiate the effectiveness and methodological advancement of incorporating optical topological priors and semantic calibration into SAR image classification and segmentation tasks.
author: Zhong Dong, Fang Xie, Xiaofei Li

title: Field-Boundary-Constrained Training for SAR Crop Type Classification: A Two-Year Assessment of Sentinel-1 Backscatter and InSAR Coherence Stability Over the Georgia Coastal Plain
content: Supervised crop type classification from synthetic aperture radar time series is typically trained on pixel-level labels from the Cropland Data Layer, which introduces contamination from noncrop pixels, such as roads, forest edges, and impervious surfaces. This study introduces a field-boundary-constrained training approach that uses crop sequence boundary polygons from the United States Department of Agriculture to restrict training and validation to verified field interiors, eliminating label noise at the source. The approach was tested across five counties in the Georgia Coastal Plain over two consecutive growing seasons, 2024 and 2025, using Sentinel-1A C-band backscatter and 12-d copolarized interferometric coherence time series. Random forest, support vector machine, and XGBoost classifiers were trained on spatially blocked splits for three crop classes: corn, cotton, and peanuts. Adding coherence to backscatter improved overall accuracy by 4.88 percentage points in 2024 and 8.29 percentage points in 2025, with gains consistent across all classifiers. The backscatter-only baseline degraded by 3.33 percentage points between years, but the combined stack remained stable, indicating that coherence acts as a temporal stabilizer when interannual backscatter variability degrades classification performance. Field-level validation using field boundaries achieved 89.76% in 2024 and 90.58% in 2025. The peanut-as-cotton misclassification rate dropped from 12.7% to 6.6% as late-season coherence pairs captured divergent crop phenologies. The results demonstrate that field-boundary-constrained training, combined with coherence augmentation, produces accurate, temporally stable crop maps suitable for operational agricultural monitoring.
author: Zach Little, Peter Webley, Alec Bennett, Cameron D. Carlson

title: Sensitivity of Ocean Bottom Pressure to Atmospheric Forcing and Vertical Resolution in Satellite Gravimetry De-Aliasing
content: In satellite gravity data processing, de-aliasing products are employed to mitigate the aliasing of high-frequency mass variations into monthly gravity field solutions. Notably, the oceanic component of de-aliasing generally exhibits larger uncertainty than the atmospheric component. However, the effects of atmospheric forcing and ocean-model vertical resolution, two key factors limiting oceanic de-aliasing performance, remain insufficiently investigated. This study quantifies their impacts on ocean bottom pressure (OBP) variability and oceanic de-aliasing. Using the LICOM3.0 ocean circulation model, we conducted three global OBP simulations with two atmospheric reanalyses (ERA5 and CRA-40) and two vertical level configurations (30 and 80 levels), resulting in the experiments ERA5-L30, ERA5-L80, and CRA-40-L80. The results show that vertical resolution generally has a greater influence than atmospheric forcing on short-period ocean mass variability. Comparison with in situ OBP records shows that long-period median RMS is more sensitive to vertical resolution than to atmospheric forcing, with broadly similar short-period results across configurations. Global mean ocean mass estimates from GRACE solutions using the LICOM3.0 products explain 94.7%–95.2% of monthly variance in the ocean-mass estimate from altimetry and Argo, compared with 93.7% when using AOD1B RL07. The Jason-2 and K-band range-acceleration comparisons show the largest differences in shallow waters, marginal seas, and semi-enclosed basins, while atmospheric forcing remains important for basin-scale agreement with altimetry and Argo. These results show that atmospheric forcing and vertical resolution directly affect ocean-mass estimates and their uncertainty, making both essential considerations for GRACE and next-generation gravity missions.
author: Yinglun Bai, Qiujie Chen, Jiahui Bai, Hailong Liu, Yunzhong Shen, Yun Xiao

title: MS-PENet: Multiscale Progressive Entropy Network for Perceptual Remote Sensing Image Compression
content: The rapid growth of high-resolution remote sensing (RS) imagery has imposed increasing demands on image compression methods that can achieve high rate–distortion (R–D) efficiency while preserving perceptually important structural and textural details. Although recent learned image compression methods have surpassed traditional codecs, they still suffer from the perception–distortion tradeoff, often generating oversmoothed reconstructions that degrade fine textures and sharp boundaries. These limitations are particularly pronounced in an RS imagery due to its large-scale scenes, repetitive patterns, and complex multifrequency characteristics. To address these challenges, we propose a multiscale progressive entropy network (MS-PENet) for perceptual RS image compression. An MS-PENet integrates frequency-aware latent representation and progressive entropy modeling into a unified end-to-end framework. Specifically, a wavelet-based latent decomposition is employed to separate multifrequency components, which are then encoded by a progressive entropy model with a hierarchical context aggregation module to capture cross-band and multiscale statistical dependencies for more accurate entropy estimation. To overcome the locality limitation of convolutional architectures, a multiscale feature refinement module based on state-space modeling is introduced to efficiently model long-range spatial dependencies with linear computational complexity. Extensive experiments on benchmark RS datasets demonstrate strong overall R–D and perceptual performance. Relative to JPEG2000, MS-PENet achieves BD-Rate savings of 43.59%, 32.35%, and 60.72% on DOTA and 31.13%, 39.50%, and 61.02% on UC-M in terms of PSNR, MS-SSIM (dB), and LPIPS, respectively. Compared with MLIC++, MS-PENet achieves LPIPS-based BD-Rate savings of 24.07% on DOTA and 19.16% on UC-M.
author: Chunyu Tan, Kai Yao, Yun Zhou, Yang Wang, Liming Zhang

title: PIFF-Net: Progressive Interaction and Foreground-Focused Fusion Network for Drone-Based RGBT Tiny Person Detection
content: Drone-based tiny person detection is important for applications, such as security surveillance and emergency rescue. While RGB-thermal (RGBT) fusion can effectively improve all-weather detection robustness, the weak tiny object features from high altitude, cross-modal feature discrepancy, and the tradeoff between information complementation and noise introduction still severely constrain detection accuracy. Therefore, we design a progressive interaction and foreground-focused fusion network (PIFF-Net), which forms a coherent pipeline of global discrepancy reduction, local propagation constraint, and then supervised foreground activation for the challenges of drone-based RGBT tiny person detection. It contains a progressive cross-modality fusion (PCF) module and a Siamese foreground enhancement (SFE) module. PCF is proposed to balance cross-modal complementation with redundancy suppression through a global-to-local progressive fusion, which consists of adaptive global frequency complementation (AGFC) module and topology-based sparse interaction (TSI) module. There, AGFC integrates dual-modal features with their frequency components multiplied by adaptively complementary weights, and TSI highlights key regions through sparse interaction guided by selectively connected topology.
