In terms of SFE, it projects dual-modal features into a shared semantic space via a Siamese architecture and a learnable pattern list, producing loss-supervised binary masks. Extensive experiments on two drone-based RGBT person detection benchmarks demonstrate that PIFF-Net achieves superior performance, especially on tiny objects, improving mAP$^{\text{tiny1}}_{\text{50}}$ by 10.2% on RGBTDronePerson and mAP$_{\text{s}}$ by 3.9% on VTUAV-det in person category.
author: Chenran Wang, Nishang Xie, Jin Ma, Jiayi Wang, Tao Zhang, Wenxian Yu

title: WAFE-T2FNet: A Sea–Land Segmentation Network Integrating Wavelet-Based Adaptive Frequency Enhancement With Type-2 Fuzzy Spatial Connections
content: Sea–land segmentation (SLS) plays a fundamental role in coastline extraction, yet complex coastal remote sensing scenes often cause ambiguous and discontinuous sea–land boundaries due to waves, intertidal zones, turbid water, shadows, and complex textured backgrounds. Meanwhile, most of the existing SLS methods mainly focus on spatial-domain representation, insufficiently exploit features from a multidomain perspective, and lack effective modeling of the uncertainty in sea–land transitional regions, making it difficult to simultaneously preserve regional semantic consistency and boundary detail representation. To address these issues, this article proposes a new SLS network, termed WAFE-T2FNet. Specifically, a wavelet-based adaptive frequency enhancement block is introduced in the decoder to enable multidomain feature learning through discrete wavelet decomposition, adaptive subband weighting, and frequency–spatial interaction, thereby enhancing boundary details and regional structural representation. In addition, a type-2 fuzzy spatial connection module is incorporated into the skip-connection pathway, where multiple candidate Gaussian fuzzy kernels and learnable secondary membership degrees are used to characterize the uncertainty of sea–land transitional regions, thereby enhancing the stability and robustness of feature fusion. Experimental results demonstrate that WAFE-T2FNet delivers superior segmentation performance over competing methods on the SLSD and L8-WBSLD datasets and exhibits promising cross-scene applicability on real Gaofen-1 scenes. Furthermore, the coastlines derived from the segmentation results of Gaofen-1 scenes in the Jiaodong Peninsula are clear and continuous, further demonstrating the practical applicability of WAFE-T2FNet. These results indicate the effectiveness of frequency enhancement and fuzzy uncertainty modeling for complex remote sensing SLS tasks.
author: Jianchao Cui, Jindong Xu, Jiantao Peng, Haoshi Cui, Jianjun Huang

title: SAR and Land Use and Land Cover Mapping: Perceptions About Multilevel Classification and Sentinel-1 Data
content: Detection and monitoring of land use and land cover changes, obtained through accurate remote sensing data, are of vital importance due to the impact of climate change and the need to implement the principles of sustainable development in modern society. In this context, this article aimed to evaluate the capacity of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data (Sentinel-1) for multilevel classification in heterogeneous landscapes. The methodology consisted of the following steps: calculation of SAR vegetation indices, analysis of variable dimensionality reduction, reduction of sample noise, and a classification process based on satellite image time series and deep learning. The results demonstrated a decrease in classification accuracy when considering scenarios with more specific thematic classes, starting from three (C1 scenario) to seven classes (C3 scenario), achieving global accuracy values of 0.999, 0.919, and 0.937, for each scenario, respectively, in training models phase. About the maps’ accuracy, the scenarios reached metrics ranging from 0.66 to 0.94. In addition, the similar volumetric backscattering behavior of different vegetative canopies in SAR data was a key parameter for the results obtained in this work.
author: José Galdino de Oliveira Júnior, Júlio César Dalla Mora Esquerdo

title: Strc: Learning Spatiotemporal Representations via Triple-Consistency for Satellite Cloud-Cover Forecasting
content: Cloud cover plays a pivotal role in solar radiation and atmospheric water cycles. Consequently, accurate cloud forecasting is indispensable for assessing radiative forcing, weather patterns, and precipitation. Recent advancements have been driven by artificial intelligence applied to satellite observations. However, prevailing autoregressive strategies suffer from cumulative error propagation, while sequence-to-sequence architectures often oversmooth high-frequency fluctuations due to coarse-grained temporal modeling, limiting their ability to capture complex cloud evolution. To address these limitations, this article proposes Strc, a spatiotemporal representation learning framework for cloud-cover forecasting. Rather than relying solely on deterministic stepwise prediction, Strc introduces consistency-guided feature regularization to improve spatiotemporal representation learning. Specifically, the framework introduces a Diversified Spatiotemporal-Contextual Construction module that constructs complementary spatiotemporal contexts via random cropping, latent feature learning, and timestamp masking. To capture fine-grained atmospheric dynamics, Strc employs a hierarchical triplet-consistency alignment objective, which regularizes representations across temporal, spatial, and instance dimensions. These components are instantiated by an efficient spatiotemporal learner that synergizes local learning, global spatial-agent learning, and temporal graph learning to capture multiscale semantics and dynamic temporal dependencies. Experiments on FY-4B satellite cloud-mask data across eight geographically and climatically diverse regions demonstrate that Strc achieves competitive or superior forecasting performance over existing baselines across multiple forecasting horizons.
author: Xiangxu Meng, Kaibin Lin, Yun Zhong, Shuai Liu, Qingfang Jiang, Wenfeng Li, Kanglian Zhao

title: R2DS-Net: A Rotation-Robust Dual Sparse Learning Network for Efficient UAV Water Body Extraction
content: Accurate water body extraction from unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery is essential for flood assessment and water resource management. However, existing deep-learning methods still struggle to handle heterogeneous water appearances, capture long-range dependencies among spatially fragmented water regions, and maintain robustness to viewpoint-induced image rotations. To address these challenges, this article proposes a lightweight rotation-robust dual sparse learning network (R2DS-Net) for UAV water body extraction. R2DS-Net adopts a dual sparse learning paradigm comprising a sparse multipath module (SMPM) and a sparse global aggregation module (SGAM). The SMPM employs feature-level sparse routing to adaptively capture diverse water appearance patterns, while the SGAM leverages Top-k sparse attention to efficiently aggregate long-range contextual information with reduced computational complexity. In addition, a circular convolution module is introduced to improve robustness to viewpoint-induced image rotations. Extensive experiments on the DroneDeploy and FloodNet datasets demonstrate that R2DS-Net consistently outperforms representative convolutional-neural-network-based, transformer-based, and lightweight methods, achieving an mean intersection over union of 91.3% with 1.3 M parameters and 1.1 GFLOPs on DroneDeploy, and 82.4% with 1.26 M parameters and 2.14 GFLOPs on FloodNet. These results show that R2DS-Net achieves an excellent balance between extraction accuracy, computational efficiency, and rotational robustness, making it highly applicable for efficient UAV water body extraction.
author: Chengzhi Deng, Zhaoming Wu, Xiaowei Sun, Shaoquan Zhang, Luqiang He, Qianhui Zhong, Fan Li, Shengqian Wang

title: Automating Linear Small Woody Feature Detection: High-Resolution Land-Cover Inputs and Geospatial Feature Segmentation in the Great Lakes Region of the United States
content: Linear small woody features (LSWFs), including windbreaks, hedgerows, and riparian woody buffers, provide ecological and agricultural functions but are poorly represented in coarse land-cover products. This study presents a multistage workflow for extracting LSWF polygons from high-resolution National Agriculture Imagery Program land cover across 35 counties in Michigan, Wisconsin, and Ohio. An established U-Net/ResNet34 land-cover package supplies the tree-canopy input; the methodological focus is the subsequent shrink-expand isolation of Trees Outside Forests, centerline cleaning and bend splitting, centerline-guided Voronoi segmentation, shape-index filtering, parent-component resolution, and regional summarization. Archive-backed sensitivity diagnostics show that candidate retention is most responsive to minimum feature length and straight and narrow feature index, while windbreak sinuosity index is influential primarily below the preserved threshold of 2.0. A structural replay of the archived workflow shows that Voronoi construction accounts for 73.97% of recorded vector-processing time, and that segmented components are selected for 1.32% of joined parent groups. The available validation record includes the completed three-county land-cover assessment and two county LSWF prediction reviews. These results bound the conclusions to the evaluated Great Lakes National Agriculture Imagery Program setting; common-reference module ablation, architecture benchmarking, and geographic transfer require separate experiments.
author: Parker A. Hopkins, Erin L. Bunting, Jack Desautel, Emily J. Silver

title: Adaptive Hierarchical and Evidential Multimodal Feature Fusion for Aerial Scene and Land-Cover Recognition Under Missing Modalities
content: In this article, we propose a multimodal adaptive hierarchical feature fusion network (AHFF-Net), a three-stage, progressive-resolution architecture that unifies four complementary mechanisms to jointly address these limitations. A spectral–spatial gating mechanism models channel-wise and spatial attention in a single, parameter-efficient formulation to suppress irrelevant channels and background regions simultaneously. Hierarchical inverted-residual dense blocks combine invertedbottleneck expansion, dense interlayer connectivity, and fire module compression to preserve fine-grained detail with a compact parameter footprint. A progressive multiresolution inception cascade extracts features across parallel receptive fields, and a semantic channel shuffle module applies content-adaptive gating with structured interleaving to resolve cross-branch feature isolation. Finally, a mixture-of-experts module with scale-specific routing decomposes intermediate features into low-, mid-, and high-frequency bands via a wavelet-inspired decomposition and routes each band to scale-specialized experts using data-driven, Frobenius-norm-based weighting. On three benchmark dataset—sMLRSNet, EuroSAT, and NWPU-12—AHFF-Net achieves classification accuracies of 95.0%, 97.0%, and 94.0%, respectively, outperforming ten pretrained convolutional neural network, transformer, and hybrid baselines while requiring roughly 20% fewer parameters. For multimodal data, we further propose REMF-Net. This multimodal evidential fusion network encodes hyperspectral, LiDAR, and SAR inputs separately, exchanges information through a center-guided similarity gate and a bottleneck fusion transformer, and combines modality-wise evidential opinions with Dempster's rule, so that it tolerates missing modalities and reports persample uncertainty. On Trento, Houston 2013, and Augsburg, REMF-Net reaches overall accuracies of 99.96%, 99.42%, and 99.40%, outperforms five recent multimodal methods, and keeps 99.10% accuracy on Augsburg when only HSI is available.
author: Muhammad John Abbas, Muhammad Attique Khan, Muhammad Sami Ullah, Fatma S. Alrayes, Mehrez Marzougui, Yunyoung Nam, Antonio Plaza

title: Structure-Guided Aerial Image Stitching via Road Semantic Topology
content: In road-dominated aerial scenes, stitching is difficult because the available features are weak, repetitive, and spatially degenerate: keypoints along road corridors form near-collinear clusters that constrain the homography only normal to the road, leaving it free to drift along the road axis. We propose a structure-guided stitching framework that uses the road semantic topology as a geometric prior. From each segmentation mask, a Hessian-based multidirectional consistency analysis extracts stable intersection nodes and road trunks and assembles them into a compact graph. These nodes act as structural anchors in a topology-constrained registration model that optimizes the homography jointly with sparse texture correspondences, suppressing drift in road regions where texture gives little constraint. A semantic-aware fusion step carries the same road-consistency constraints into the seam blending. On the Massachusetts Roads Dataset, the method matches or exceeds the classical baselines (scale-invariant feature transform+RANSAC and as-projective-as-possible) on the alignment metrics, and the deep baselines (unsupervised deep homography and LoFTR) also degrade on weak-texture pairs. Ablation and sensitivity studies confirm the contribution of each module. The topology prior is a safeguard for the degraded regime rather than a general improvement: neutral when texture is strong, decisive when it weakens. When texture-based registration degrades (e.g., image blur or weak texture), the road masks—unaffected by the degradation—supply a dense structural cue that recovers the pairwise geometry through pattern matching in the overlap band, cutting the mean placement error by up to $7.6\times$ under controlled blur with ground-truth masks—an upper bound.
author: Wei Wu, Zhengyu Liu, Shuting Yang, Dong Sun, Cong Ma, Xia Yuan

title: Modulated Deformable Fully Convolutional Network for Object Detection of Multiscale Open-Pit Mining Area in China
content: Utilizing extensive satellite remote sensing images for precise and reliable object detection in open-pit mining areas is fundamental to high-quality ecological development. However, such detection faces challenges: high texture similarity between objects and surrounding background complicates identification, and insufficient multi-scale samples in existing datasets weaken model generalization. We constructed two dedicated multi-scale datasets, NOMA and SOMA, from highresolution imagery covering approximately 160,000 km2 in northern and southern China, and proposed a modulated deformable fully convolutional network (MDFC RCNN) for multi-scale open-pit mining area detection. Its core uses modulated deformable convolution (MDC) for adaptive geometric deformation, dynamically adjusting sampling locations to capture critical geometric features of irregular mining shapes. A fully convolutional region proposal network (FCRPN) integrates multi-scale predictions within a feature pyramid to detect objects of varying sizes. By synergizing MDC and FCRPN, the fusion and enhancement of features across distinct scales are achieved, consequently improving the detection accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed network outperforms 13 comparative Faster R-CNNseries object detection models across all four metrics in open-pit mining scenarios. The average precision (AP50) of the proposed network on the NOMA and SOMA datasets exceeds that of the suboptimal counterpart by 3.216% and 2.295%, respectively. Spatial transferability experiments at locations not covered by these datasets demonstrated spatial transferability. The network reliably captures the full spatial extent of irregularly bounded open-pit mining areas, supporting sustainable mining management and ecological restoration. The datasets and model code are available at https://github.com/RSIDEA-ECUT/MDFC-R-CNN.
author: Xunqiang Gong, Jintao Wu, Yufeng Zhu, Xinyu Zhou, Zhenqi Liu, Liqin Cao, Chuan Zhang, Ailong Ma, Yanfei Zhong

title: RGRT-MODEL: A Rice Crop Radiative Transfer Model for Seed Organs
content: Radiative transfer modeling is a central tool for accurate inversion of crop growth information. Existing models mostly focus on the leaf or canopy scale and have not yet considered the contribution of seeds to the collected spectra. Observations have shown that the contribution of seeds to the canopy spectrum becomes more and more obvious as the grains mature in the later stages of rice development. However, there are significant differences in the physical characteristics and traits between seeds and leaves, and none of the existing models can meet the simulation needs of the optical properties of the seeds. For this purpose, this study has newly designed and developed a 3-D rice grain radiative transfer model, RGRT-MODEL, which characterizes the 3-D structure of rice grains by constructing a 3-D ellipsoidal space and establishing 3-D ellipsoidal space equations in combination with the ellipsoidal morphological characteristics of rice grains. The core theories of geometric optics and physical optics are introduced to clarify the optical parameters of the surface interface and internal medium of the model. The analytical expressions for the optical properties of the model in forward simulation are derived by combining the interaction process between light and the ellipsoidal seed model. A two-stage optimization strategy of “global search and local fine optimization” is adopted to calibrate the absorption coefficient and refractive index of the internal medium. The tracking statistics of reflectance and transmittance are realized with the help of the ray tracing method. The reflectance and transmittance spectra of the samples in the validation dataset were simulated using the RGRT-MODEL and compared with the measured values. The results showed that the mean absolute error of each band of simulated reflectance, transmittance, and absorbance for all varieties of seeds was ranging from 0.006–0.061, and the roots mean square error (RMSEs) of simulated spectra for over 95% of individual samples are less than 0.1, and the RMSEs of simulated spectra for over 95% of individual samples were less than 0.1, indicating that the model reproduced the measured grain-level spectra reasonably well across the tested varieties. The proposed RGRT-MODEL provides an effective grain-scale framework for analyzing the optical response of rice seeds under the assumptions of idealized ellipsoidal geometry and an effective homogeneous internal medium.
author: Yan Sun, Shuang Xiang, Sinuo Chen, Jingyi Zhang, Hao Wen, Hanrui Guo, Mengqi Li, Weijian Zhang, Yingli Cao, Fenghua Yu

title: HEFFNet: A Hierarchical Multimodal Feature Enhancement–Fusion–Feedback Network for Remote Sensing Image Semantic Segmentation
content: Cloud occlusion and the substantial heterogeneity between optical and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) modalities severely limit the robustness and stability of optical–SAR multimodal semantic segmentation in complex remote sensing scenes. The fundamental disparities in image formation mechanisms—between optical texture features and SAR scattering properties—cause current cross-modal fusion approaches to suffer from semantic inconsistency and modality incompatibility, resulting in unclear object boundaries and misclassification in intricate scenes. To address these issues, this article proposes a hierarchical enhancement–fusion–feedback network (HEFFNet), which serves as a modular enhancement framework for complex optical–SAR semantic segmentation scenarios. At each encoding stage, HEFFNet sequentially performs an enhancement–fusion–feedback process. First, a difference-guided feature enhancement module is designed to enhance modality-specific feature representations using cross-modal difference information, thereby reducing intermodal feature interference. Then, a tri-level cross-modal fusion module is proposed to adaptively model the complementary relationship between optical and SAR features through semantic-, spatial-, and channel-level collaborative interactions, improving the semantic consistency and discriminability of the fused features. Furthermore, a fusion-guided feedback module is introduced to feed effective information from fused features into the next encoding stage, enabling progressive refinement of multilevel semantic representations. Experiments are conducted on public OPT–SAR datasets, including WHU-OPT-SAR, PIE-RGB-SAR, and YESeg-OPT-SAR, and model robustness is further evaluated on a synthetic cloud-degradation extension based on PIE-RGB-SAR. The experimental results show that HEFFNet achieves stable performance improvements in regular optical–SAR semantic segmentation scenarios and exhibits good robustness under synthetic cloud degradation and complex land-cover conditions.
author: Junqi Zhao, Min Chen, Wei Guo, Wen Li, Jinbo Zhang, Qing Zhu, Han Hu, Xuming Ge, Bo Xu

title: SPFR-SAM: Shadow-Prior Feature Reconstruction With SAM-Guided Encoding for Side-Scan Sonar Small-Target Detection
content: In side-scan sonar (SSS) imagery, targets and their accompanying shadows are spatially coupled with ambiguous boundaries, while backgrounds are dominated by speckle noise and target-to-clutter contrast remains extremely low, rendering reliable pixel-level small-target detection a persistent challenge in mine-hunting applications. To address these challenges, we propose SPFR-SAM, a shadow-prior feature reconstruction (SPFR) framework augmented with segment anything model (SAM)-guided encoding for SSS small-target detection. SPFR-SAM integrates a consult-guided MiM encoder, the cross-channel contextual semantic interaction (CCSI) module, and a shadow-prior-guided decoding pipeline to jointly model small targets and their shadows. This pipeline is implemented by the shadow-prior feature reconstruction module, which embeds shadow priors derived from side-scan sonar imaging physics into multiscale feature reconstruction to refine target–shadow boundaries and improve pixel-level detection accuracy. In addition, CCSI captures lateral contextual information and cross-channel semantic dependencies, with particular attention to the lateral semantic relations between targets and their shadows, thereby strengthening small-target representations under complex seafloor backgrounds. Furthermore, we manually annotate pixel-level masks for the public MOD and Cylinder2 datasets, providing benchmarks for SSS small-target detection. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework; on the Cylinder2 dataset, SPFR-SAM achieves an intersection over union of 53.15% and an F1-score of 69.41%, substantially outperforming existing state-of-the-art small-target detection methods. The code is available available online.
author: Yinghua Song, Guanying Huo, Simon X. Yang, Zhen Cheng, Weifeng Kong

title: Quality Control of Sentinel-1 Doppler Current Products Affected by Local Strong-Scattering Target Contamination
content: Spaceborne synthetic aperture radar Doppler frequency shifts provide high-spatial-resolution observations for ocean surface current retrieval, but ships, offshore platforms, buoys, and other nongeophysical strong scatterers can produce local anomalies. This study proposes a quality-control and Doppler-field reconstruction method for local strong-scattering target contamination in Sentinel-1 Level-2 ocean surface current (OCN) products. An integrated index constructed from normalized radar cross section and Doppler-estimation standard deviation identifies contaminated pixels; morphological dilation constrains the reconstruction mask, and local ordinary kriging estimates the missing Doppler values. Across 131 scenes, the scene-level median Doppler standard deviation, range, and mean spatial gradient within the adaptive evaluation region decrease from 17.27 to 12.70 Hz, 306.53 to 113.45 Hz, and 5.83 to 2.60 Hz/pixel, respectively. In strictly paired comparisons, the pixel-pooled root mean square error (RMSE) against HF radar decreases from 0.573 to 0.414 m/s (83 scenes), and that against hybrid coordinate ocean model (HYCOM) decreases from 0.631 to 0.492 m/s (92 scenes). The output retains a reconstruction mask, method flag, and kriging variance. The method is a reproducible quality-control step for locally contaminated Doppler products, while reconstructed values remain estimates rather than direct observations.
author: Zhonghao Yang, Hanghang Yang, Jiahao Liu, Meng Zhang, Xiaodong Cui, Ruifu Wang

title: Progressive Cross-Modal Alignment and Interaction via Transformer for Multimodal Remote Sensing Image Classification
content: Hyperspectral imagery provides rich spectral information, while light detection and ranging data offer precise geometric structure. Fusing these complementary modalities can substantially improve land-cover classification accuracy. However, achieving effective fusion is challenging due to significant modal heterogeneity and inconsistent feature scales. Here, we propose a progressive alignment and cross-modal transformer network (PACTNet) to address these issues. The model introduces an iterative cross-modal alignment module that progressively aligns cross-modal features from the structural level to the semantic level through layerwise interactions. A dual-tokenization strategy subsequently maps these aligned features into local and global token representations, which are processed by a Transformer encoder augmented with a locality-enhanced feedforward network to inject spatial inductive bias without compromising global modeling. For final fusion, a gated cross-modal attention mechanism adaptively integrates cross-modal information using bidirectional cross-attention with a learnable gating function. Evaluated on four public datasets, PACTNet achieves superior performance, with overall accuracy reaching 98.71% on Houston2013 and 95.43% on Augsburg, outperforming ten state-of-the-art methods. The model also maintains a low parameter count (0.30–0.34 M) and computational cost (0.042 G FLOPs), demonstrating a favorable balance between accuracy and efficiency. These results underscore the effectiveness of progressive feature alignment and adaptive gating in exploiting multimodal remote sensing data for precise and robust classification.
author: Mengyao Yang, Uzair Aslam Bhatti, Dekai Li, Mengxing Huang, Abdulmohsen Algarni, Leila Jamel, Faheem Ullah Khan, Khayrulla Urozboev, Shakhboz Meylikulov, Sardor Sabirov

title: Classification and Mapping of Wetlands in the Coastal Lowlands of the State of Rio De Janeiro, Brazil, Using Optical and SAR Time Series Data
content: This research addresses the importance of wetland conservation in Brazil, specifically in the state of Rio de Janeiro, where a history of anthropogenic interventions and urban expansion threaten these ecosystems. This study aims to map and characterize the wetlands in the coastal lowlands of Rio de Janeiro according to their flood-pulse regime, using a synergistic multitemporal approach between radar (Sentinel-1) and optical (Sentinel-2) data. The methodology employed the random forest algorithm in the Google Earth Engine environment to process temporal image cubes from 2019 to 2021, integrated through spatial and temporal segmentation of geo-objects. The results indicated that wetlands occupy approximately 31.2% of the study area, with 24.9% represented by temporary flood wetlands (5.4% occasionally flooded and 19.5% frequently flooded) and 6.3% by permanently flooded wetlands. The classification using synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data achieved an overall accuracy of 98%, while the multispectral instrument (MSI) optical data yielded an overall accuracy of 87%. The integration of SAR and MSI data for mapping wetland flooding regimes achieved an overall accuracy of 88%. This research contributes to the scientific field of remote sensing by demonstrating the effectiveness of multisensor integration in detecting fragmented and dynamic ecosystems, providing an unprecedented inventory that serves as technical support for restoration and land use planning strategies in tropical regions under urban pressure.
author: Evelyn de Castro Porto Costa, Raul Sanchez Vicens

title: Multisource Scattering Prior Injection and Routing for Fine-Grained SAR Aircraft Detection
content: Fine-grained aircraft detection in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images remains a highly challenging task. Most existing methods for fine-grained. From the mechanism of microwaveSAR aircraft detection typically rely on conventional optical detection paradigms. However, the traditional vision networks lack physical perception of microwave scattering characteristics, thereby failing to explicitly exploit the intrinsic structural characteristics and electromagnetic scattering priors of SAR imagery. Furthermore, conventional feature extractors fail to capture the inherent anisotropy of SAR targets and their orientation-dependent discrete structures, leading to incomplete structural representation and increased confusion among highly similar categories. To address these limitations, we propose MSP-RANet, a physics-guided framework that integrates multisource scattering prior encoding and adaptive feature routing. Specifically, we first design a physical prior injection module (PPIM) to explicitly encode scattering priors into a multichannel representation, including scattering point and structural information, and integrate them with visual features via residual attention fusion. Second, we design a scattering-aware routing convolution (SAR-Conv) to capture anisotropic and discrete scattering structures under varying orientations through dynamic routing of orthogonal and diagonal branches. Finally, a hard negative repulsion (HNR) loss is proposed to enhance inter-class separability by enlarging decision margins between highly similar categories. This comprehensive framework—incorporating physical priors, scattering-aware routing, and feature boundary repulsion—provides a novel perspective for fine-grained aircraft detection. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms the baseline YOLOv11 s network, achieving mAP@0.5 improvements of 1.0% and 6.0% on the SAR-AIRcraft-1.0 and FAIR-CSAR-V1.0 datasets, respectively.
author: Jian Chen, Weikang Jian, Xiaoding Zhou, Jiayi Yuan, Ying Liang, Yuxiao Qin, Yali Zong, Zhongling Huang

title: Attention-Based Co-Estimation of Lightning Position and Frequency From Satellite Data With Bias Calibration
content: Estimating lightning location and frequency from geostationary meteorological satellite observations and topographic data can complement lightning monitoring under data-limited conditions; however, sparse positive samples, a dominant zero-valued background, and a long-tailed frequency distribution increase the difficulty of continuous-field modeling. This study constructs a nine-channel input from eight Himawari-8/9 Advanced Himawari Imager features and one digital elevation model feature and grids the Very Low Frequency Lightning-Location Network records into lightning frequency fields with a spatial resolution of 2 km and a temporal resolution of 10 min, in which the nonzero spatial support and pixel values represent lightning locations and frequencies, respectively. For this sparse-regression task, an FE-UNet integrating channel attention, mask attention, attention-gate-guided skip connections, and Gaussian masked MSE is developed. In the 2-km main experiment, FE-UNet achieves a probability of detection of 0.7840 and a critical success index of 0.6036, with global and positive-only root-mean-square error values of 0.4277 and 5.8909, respectively, demonstrating superior overall performance to the comparison models. Continuous piecewise calibration adjusts the positive-only mean bias error on the test set from $-$2.0186 to 0.5616, brings the aggregated response in high-frequency intervals closer to the corresponding recorded values, and produces moderate overestimation for some low- and moderate-frequency samples, thereby exhibiting a frequency-dependent scale-adjustment characteristic. The 5-km controlled incremental experiments show that convective available potential energy and 850–500 hPa bulk wind shear provide incremental information for some regression and lightning-location identification metrics, respectively, although the additional environmental variables do not yield simultaneous improvements across all metrics. These results indicate that satellite–topographic data can serve as a data-driven complement to ground-based detection, radar observations, and physics-based numerical simulations for lightning-location and frequency monitoring.
author: Yi Liu, Xinjue Wang, Yuanpeng Han, Lin Song, Zirui Xu, Jialei Wang, Qilin Zhang, Min Xia, Wei Zhuang

title: Change Decoupling Enhancement Network for Remote Sensing Change Detection
content: In remote sensing change detection tasks, pseudochanges caused by unchanged noise represent the most typical source of interference. The disturbances originating from unchanged backgrounds cause pseudochanges and real land-cover changes to be highly entangled in the feature space, which severely affects the ability of network to identify true changes. To address this issue, we propose a change decoupling enhancement network (CDENet), which improves change detection from the perspectives of feature decoupling and semantic enhancement. Specifically, the proposed change representation decoupling module computes the spatial similarity between bi-temporal features to explicitly identify and separate unchanged components, thereby obtaining purer and more stable change representations. Furthermore, a semantic consistency enhancement module is introduced, which divides the feature channels into multiple groups and independently models multiscale spatial cues and within-group channel relationships to enhance the discriminability and spatial coherence of change representations. Experiments conducted on the LEVIR-CD, WHU-CD, and SYSU-CD datasets show that CDENet achieves strong results by effectively eliminating interference from unchanged features.
author: Xu Zhang, Yue Du, Yan Zhou, Kaihua Zhang

title: A Vision–Language and Knowledge-Graph Reasoning Framework for Semantic UAV Remote Sensing Image Retrieval, Interpretation, and Interaction
content: Uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) remote sensing provides high-resolution spatial information for site monitoring, infrastructure planning, environmental observation, and facility management. However, conventional task-specific analysis and similarity-based vision–language retrieval offer limited support for open-ended querying, structured domain knowledge, spatial reasoning, and explainable decision support. This study proposes a vision–language and knowledge-graph framework that integrates semantic representation, natural-language-driven image-level and region-level retrieval, structured knowledge representation, and rule-based reasoning. Vision–language models align UAV imagery with textual queries, while the knowledge graph organizes objects, spatial relations, engineering constraints, and safety rules. The retrieval stage identifies semantically relevant scenes and regions, and the reasoning stage evaluates explicit constraints and produces traceable explanations for interactive interpretation. As a preliminary proof of concept, LoveDA ground-truth semantic masks are converted into planning-oriented cost maps and evaluated using A$^{*}$-based path planning. The results show that structured semantic scene information can be transformed into an actionable spatial representation for downstream decision support. The current experiment validates one representative semantic-information-to-decision pathway; full end-to-end evaluation of the vision–language retrieval and knowledge-graph reasoning modules remains future work.
author: Hsin-Te Wu

title: ViSARA: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of Visual–Geometry Foundation Models for Cloud-Obscured Earth Observation Reconstruction
content: Cloud-obscured Earth observation(EO) reconstruction is important for recovering usable three-dimensional information when atmospheric conditions make parts of an optical satellite image unavailable. The problem couples three requirements: evidence reliability varies across views, foundation-scale geometry models are expensive to specialize, and missing-evidence recovery must generalize across cloud conditions. We present ViSARA, a compact adapter for a frozen VGGT-family visual–geometry foundation model. To prevent weak observations from dominating dense surface prediction, ViSARA estimates cross-view feature support, forms a reliability-weighted consensus, and applies gated residual repair. To retain the pretrained geometry pathway at low adaptation cost, one identity-initialized adapter is shared across the four backbone stages consumed by the dense head, leaving only 0.024% of the model parameters trainable. To avoid dependence on cloud-specific training masks, generic corruption distillation uses structured token and whole-view dropout to recover clean teacher representations from incomplete EO observations. Across the complete five-fold spatially held-out protocol, ViSARA reduces mean camera-aligned Chamfer distance from 143.924 to 137.916, a 4.174% reduction. Component ablations further reduce Chamfer by 1.724 relative to unweighted consensus and by 1.678 relative to local residual repair, while matched profiling shows only 1.95% additional peak memory and 4.14% additional median model latency over the frozen path. These results demonstrate parameter-efficient cross-view repair across controlled synthetic cloud conditions. Real-cloud evaluation further tests the method under atmospheric obstruction, while full-model inference requires substantial memory and time.
author: Yifan Liu, Mingke Xing, Bin Peng, Tong Hua, Guo Zhao, Jincai Chen

title: TMo-VSR: Temporally Modulated Heterogeneous Spatial Experts for Satellite Video Super-Resolution
content: Satellite video super-resolution provides high-resolution spatiotemporal information for dynamic Earth observation and supports downstream tasks, such as disaster monitoring, traffic analysis, and object tracking. However, satellite videos contain highly heterogeneous land-cover contents and region-dependent temporal dynamics. Conventional unified temporal fusion or single spatial modeling methods are difficult to adapt to such diverse spatiotemporal regions, since global structures, local continuity, and fine details often require different reconstruction mechanisms. To address this problem, we propose TMo-VSR, a temporally modulated heterogeneous spatial mixture-of-experts model for satellite video super-resolution. The key idea is to formulate reconstruction as an adaptive divide-and-conquer process, where different expert networks are dynamically activated according to region-specific spatial contents and temporal variations, enabling more targeted reconstruction for heterogeneous satellite scenes. Specifically, we design a temporal modulation router to aggregate temporal correlations between current and historical frames and generate pixelwise time-varying weights for adaptive expert allocation. We further introduce a global–local–detail mixture-of-experts module, which employs global, local, and detail experts to model long-range structural dependencies, neighborhood-continuous patterns, and fine textures or small objects, respectively. In the global branch, an axial attention global expert is adopted to efficiently capture long-range dependencies with reduced computational cost. Through temporal modulation and spatial expert specialization, TMo-VSR improves spatiotemporal consistency and detail restoration. Experiments on two satellite video super-resolution datasets demonstrate that TMo-VSR achieves the best peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) on both Jilin-189 and SAT-MTB-VSR, as well as the best structural similarity on Jilin-189. In particular, on the Jilin-189 dataset, TMo-VSR improves the average PSNR by 0.19 dB over existing methods.
author: Mohan Yang, Bowen Chen, Songru Yang, Liqin Liu, Zhengxia Zou, Zhenwei Shi

title: Morphology-Guided Learning for Complex Scenes Flood Boundary Detection and Mapping With SAR Image
content: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery is widely used for rapid flood mapping because of its all-weather and day–night observation capability. However, SAR-based flood extraction remains challenging in complex flood scenes, where speckle noise, heterogeneous backscatter from urban or vegetated areas, and fragmented inundation patterns often degrade mapping accuracy. To address these challenges, this article proposes DSPC-Net, a dual-stream and connectivity-preserving framework for SAR flood mapping. DSPC-Net integrates a dual-stream encoder block and a Local-Context Skip Connection module to capture both large-scale hydrological context and fine-scale boundary information. A two-stage training strategy, combining masked image modeling pretraining with morphology-guided multitask supervision, is further introduced to improve flood representation learning. Experiments on the STURM-Flood dataset show that DSPC-Net achieves an IoU of 71.28% and an F1-score of 83.23%, outperforming several representative segmentation networks. Zero-shot transfer experiments on Sen1Floods11 achieve an IoU of 62.88% and an F1-score of 77.21%, demonstrating effective cross-dataset transfer. Overall, the results demonstrate improved segmentation and structural quality on STURM-Flood, together with effective cross-dataset transfer to Sen1Floods11.
author: Mengyao Wang, Ning Zhang, Sunwen Du, Song Chang, Xicheng Tan

title: Semisupervised Great Wall Relic Trace Extraction via Scene-Level Adapter and Relic-Oriented Consistency Learning
content: Great Wall relic extraction from high-resolution remote sensing (RS) imagery supports large-area archaeological investigation and heritage conservation but is constrained by costly pixel-level annotations. Semisupervised segmentation reduces annotation requirements by exploiting unlabeled imagery, yet diverse relic-bearing environments hinder scene adaptation and weak, narrow relic traces compromise feature-level consistency learning. To address these challenges, we propose a semisupervisedGreat Wall relic segmentation framework with two complementary adaptation mechanisms for improving relic scene adaptation and feature consistency learning under limited annotation conditions. First, a scene-level adapter is integrated into the frozen DINOv2 encoder to capture scene context information and generate scene-adapted embeddings, improving its robustness across diverse relic-bearing environments. Second, relic-oriented consistency learning derives relic-oriented features through two trainable replicated transformer blocks. For unlabeled images, hierarchical complementary dropout is applied to both scene-adapted and relic-oriented features to enforce feature-level consistency and improve the perception of weak and elongated relic traces. In addition, a contour-guided progressive reweighting strategy is introduced to incorporate contour information into the unsupervised loss, adaptively adjusting pseudolabel supervision for ambiguous relic boundaries in unlabeled images. Experiments on three multiregion Great Wall relic datasets demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms representative semisupervised segmentation and road extraction methods under different labeling ratios. Under the 5% labeling ratio, it achieves centerline-based quality scores of 0.6519, 0.8245, and 0.4604 on the Hebei Great Wall Relic, Beijing Great Wall Relic, and Gansu Great Wall Relic datasets, respectively. This study provides a practical semisupervised solution for large-area archaeological relic identification.
author: Daoyuan Zheng, Shaohua Wang, Haixia Feng, Tiancheng Liu, Rui Xu, Shunli Wang, Mingyao Ai, Pengcheng Zhao, Zhipeng Chen, Qingwu Hu

title: Lunar-Based Cross-Calibration of GF-4 Mid-Infrared Band: Establishing a Radiometric Link From FY-4B/AGRI
content: Gaofen-4 (GF-4), as China's first geostationary high-resolution imaging satellite, carries a mid-infrared (MIR) channel that is critical for monitoring high-temperature targets such as active fires. However, GF-4 lacks an onboard calibrator. Site-based calibration primarily targets the low-gain, long-exposure (15 ms) observation mode, leaving a calibration gap for the high-gain, short-exposure (4 ms) mode. Leveraging the high spectral similarity of the co-orbital FY-4B satellite, this article establishes a MIR lunar radiometric transfer link to perform on-orbit radiometric cross-calibration for the GF-4 MIR channel. The framework employs 59 FY-4B/AGRI lunar observations as the radiometric reference, 9 GF-4/IRS observations for calibration, and 19 historical HIRS observations for independent validation. Quantitative signal decoupling indicates that thermal emission dominates the MIR budget (>83%), with solar reflection contributing ≤16.7%. The results show that the coefficient of determination (R2) of the calibration equation reached 0.9951, with a root mean square error of 0.1528 W/m2/μm/sr. Accuracy assessment shows that the proposed method reduces the overall median absolute relative error from 24.5% to 3.3%. Specifically, at large phase angles (≈114°), the brightness temperature deviation is reduced from +32.4 K (using the traditional thermophysical model) to -5.8 K. Furthermore, the calibrated lunar surface brightness temperature distribution agrees well with the $T \propto \text{co}{{\mathrm{s}}^{0.163}}\theta $ model. This article addresses the calibration gap for the GF-4 high-gain mode and provides an on-orbit calibration approach for the MIR channels of geostationary payloads without requiring additional onboard hardware.
author: Yunkai Xu, Yunzhao Wu, Ling Sun, Zhiwei Wang, Yong Zhang

title: From Partial Disclosures to Scaling Evidence for Earth Observation Foundation Models
content: Earth-observation (EO) foundation models are increasingly relevant to long-horizon choices about sensing, archives, downlink, ground processing, and onboard or near-sensor inference. These choices depend not only on benchmark scores, but on evidence about how EO model performance changes with model scale, data exposure, compute, adaptation protocol, and deployment cost. Public EO foundation-model releases, however, are not organized as controlled scaling experiments: they combine heterogeneous benchmark tables, partial training-scale summaries, ambiguous parameter semantics, and incomplete compute or inference-cost reporting. This article treats that incompleteness as an object of analysis. We construct a disclosure observability registry for public EO and EO-linked foundation-model families, coding scaling-relevant quantities as reported, derived, partial, missing, or not applicable, and translate the audit into an EO scaling-disclosure checklist. The registry then defines which model-family benchmark groups in the public record are comparable enough to support a bounded shape-test case study. The result is an audit-to-analysis account of what current disclosures can support, what they cannot support, and what future releases would need to report to enable stronger parameter, data, compute, and deployment-cost forecasts for EO artificial intelligence and related space-infrastructure planning.
author: Tyler Cody, Hyunglok Kim, Venkataraman Lakshmi, Peter A. Beling

title: A Framework for Crop Classification Using van Zyl Type Polarization Signature and Modified DenseNet Architecture
content: For a given synthetic aperture radar (SAR) sensor configuration, the polarization signature (PS) (van Zyl type) provides a comprehensive view of the target scatterer. It is a mathematical descriptor that can, in principle, provide a better target characterization than a traditional polarimetric SAR (PolSAR) decomposition. However, PS is associated with challenges such as significant intraclass variability, rendering it difficult to use directly within a classification framework. Current machine learning techniques have the ability to discriminate target pixels based on learning from a sufficient amount of field data, in scenarios where such data are available. In this work, we pair the rich information in PS with the power and versatility of a supervised deep learning model (modified DenseNet) to devise a novel framework for multicrop classification. PolSAR data from the NASA-ISRO joint campaign of L- and S-band airborne SAR (LS-ASAR), acquired over an agricultural region in Arkansas, are used to solve a multicrop discrimination problem. We also compare this framework, head-to-head, with other classification models making use of either SAR backscatter (amplitude) data or the popular Yamaguchi four-component decomposition with rotation of the coherency matrix (Y4R) followed by a Random Forest (RF) or a DenseNet classifier. Multifrequency extension to the proposed methodology is also carried out and the results are compared with the single frequency framework. The framework for utilizing the dual-frequency PS achieved an overall accuracy of 94.1%, considerably higher than other models, with an F1-score of 93.9% indicating high confidence.
author: Tarun Maganti, Sanid Chirakkal, Rosly. Boi Lyngdoh, Deepak Putrevu

title: Rapid Shrinkage of Global Oceanic Pseudoinvariant Calibration Sites: Associated Factors, Potential Mechanisms, and Implications for Satellite Data Quality
content: Oceanic pseudoinvariant calibration sites (PICS) are widely treated as optically stable references for multi-decadal vicarious calibration of satellite ocean color records. Whether that optical stability holds under changing ocean–atmosphere conditions remains insufficiently tested; if overlooked, environmental change in these waters can be absorbed into updated sensor gains and aliased into long-term ocean color records. We therefore use the monthly Comprehensive Score Metric (CSM), derived primarily from MODIS-Aqua (2003–2023), to assess long-term oceanic calibration-site stability—a macroscale question distinct from day-scale vicarious calibration. Terra contributes only to the three subindicators that compare the Aqua and Terra overpass times within a day. After seasonal-cycle removal, global radiometric stability declines significantly (Sen's slope=$-0.0015\,\text{yr}^{-1}$; modified Mann–Kendall $p = 7.4\times 10^{-10}$), and the annual ocean fraction with CSM$\,>\,$0.6 falls from 33.4% to 23.0%, indicating contraction of waters suitable for high-precision calibration. Random Forest score decomposition identifies diurnal volatility of surface wind speed as the dominant contributor to CSM variability, consistent with wind–optical coupling via roughness, whitecaps, and backscattering. In the equatorial Pacific, El Niño-Southern Oscillation is associated with strong stability losses, including a 26% reduction in Niño-3.4 regional-mean CSM during the 2015/2016 El Niño. These climate-linked declines raise concern for ocean-color product quality and for studies that depend on those products. We find a negative co-variation between CSM and MODIS-Aqua Rrs validation error that is not yet causally attributed, yet already indicates that oceanic PICS should be treated as dynamic, climate-sensitive calibration references.
author: Xiaofan Wang, Jun Chen, Mengqi Zhang

title: Vision–Language Foundation Models for Remote Sensing: A Survey of Open-Vocabulary Perception, Multimodal Reasoning, and Generation
content: Vision–language foundation models (VLFMs) are extending remote sensing beyond fixed-label prediction to natural-language interaction, localized perception, multimodal reasoning, and language-conditioned generation. Yet fluent answers and plausible images do not by themselves show that outputs are supported by observations. Existing reviews tend to organize studies by architecture or task, leaving capability, evidence, and evaluation conditions insufficiently connected. This survey synthesizes remote sensing vision–language research and distinguishes core methods from enabling models, datasets, benchmarks, and prior reviews. It examines architectures and domain adaptation, then organizes capabilities into three complementary families: open-vocabulary perception, multimodal reasoning, and generative processing. Across these families, differences in spatial scale, geography, prompts, data splits, sensors, and external tools make reported results difficult to compare and their supporting evidence difficult to inspect. The survey traces the field's shift from global image–text alignment toward localized perception, structured reasoning, multisource integration, and language-conditioned generation. It then develops an assessment framework that links capabilities to their evidence and evaluation conditions, supporting model comparison, benchmark design, and the formulation of readiness criteria. The framework provides a basis for assessment; it does not establish that current systems are ready for deployment.
author: Wenchao Zhang, Wenhui Ye, Zhenhua Yu, Jun Mou, Fa Zhu, Junxin Chen

title: MCSA-YOLO: Retraining-Free Cross-Altitude Generalization for Dense Cabbage Detection in Multimodal UAV Imagery
content: Accurate crop detection and counting are essential for precision agriculture, yet variations in uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) flight altitude substantially alter image resolution, target scale, and spectral characteristics, limiting cross-altitude model generalization. This study developed a multimodal UAV cabbage detection dataset comprising RGB, four-band multispectral (MS), and RGB–MS Fusion imagery acquired at 30 and 80 m, with 154,214 verified instance annotations. A cross-altitude evaluation protocol was established by training on 30 m imagery and directly testing on 80 m imagery from geographically independent fields, assessing generalization under combined altitude and field variations. We proposed MCSA-YOLO, a retraining-free cross-altitude detection framework integrating a lightweight spectral–spatial object-aware attention module (MODA-Lite) into YOLO11s and a modality-aware spatial–spectral degradation augmentation strategy. The augmentation simulates realistic spatial resolution loss and spectral perturbations across different modalities to enhance robustness to altitude-induced distribution shifts. On the 30 m test set, MCSA-YOLO achieved an F1 score of 93.46%, with 1,206 false negatives. Under direct 30-to-80 m transfer, it improved F1 from 76.07% to 81.46% and reduced false negatives from 8,489 to 5,221 compared with YOLO11s. With degradation augmentation, F1 and recall further increased to 87.33% and 90.76%, respectively, reducing false negatives to 2,601. Ablation results indicated that degradation augmentation contributed most to cross-altitude robustness, while MODA-Lite provided additional modality-dependent improvements. These findings establish a practical benchmark and framework for robust UAV-based crop detection across flight altitudes.
author: Yuekai Zhao, Peize Wu, Jie Deng, Zhaowei Zhu, Zhenqing Yang, Jingxue Chang, Yingzhen Ge, Canran Chen, Danfeng Hong

title: CCARE: A Cross-Cognition Aware Semantic Segmentation Network for Road Extraction Under Imperfect Supervision
content: Road extraction is a fundamental task in remote sensing image interpretation. However, the complexity of road morphology and cognitive bias in manual annotation inevitably introduce noise information into training data, causing models to learn from imperfect supervision. Existing noise-label learning methods mainly rely on one-stage supervision optimization and lack the ability to actively assess and continuously refine supervision credibility. To address this issue, this article proposes a cognitive aware road extraction method, termed CCARE, which enables cognitive formation, cognitive assessment, cognitive optimization, throughout the training process for dynamic utilization of noise information. Specifically, CCARE employs a dual-decoder architecture with differential attention to construct complementary road cognition. Prediction cognitive credibility assessment is then exploited to estimate supervision credibility, allowing the model to prioritize reliable supervision progressively. Furthermore, cognitive perturbation and cross-view consistency are introduced to continuously calibrate cognitive bias, recover missing road information, enhancing structural representation in complex scenes. Extensive experiments on three benchmark road extraction datasets demonstrate that CCARE outperforms existing noise-label learning methods in both quantitative metrics and visual quality, with performance even surpassing conventional fully supervised methods in some cases, provide a new learning paradigm for road extraction under imperfect supervision in future.
